text:
GLM-5.3 > GLM-5.4

雷霆思考之神诞生，今天 GLM-5.4 发布第一天，我拿它和 GLM-5.3、DeepSeek 做了一次后端任务实测，没有达到预期，评价拉完了

同一个 Android APK 逆向去广告任务，分别交给 DeepSeek V4.1 Flash、GLM-5.3 和 GLM-5.4，使用相同的 APK 和需求，完整考察逆向分析、代码修改、打包和验证能力

先抛开首发当天的算力和重试问题，GLM-5.4 最大的问题是过度思考，以及由此带来的任务发散

1️⃣ GLM-5.3：1 小时 9 分钟，完成交付

134 次模型请求，136 次工具调用，零重试

定位 WindMill 广告聚合 SDK，修改 10 个广告加载和展示方法，完成 APK 回编译、签名和静态验证，最终交付 41.8 MB 的 APK

方案比较直接，虽然回调处理和资源重编译存在一定风险，但任务收敛很快，执行效率不错

2️⃣ DeepSeek V4.1 Flash：1 小时 28 分钟，完成交付

108 次模型请求，134 次工具调用，仅重试 1 次

同时修改 App 广告封装层、底层 SDK 和 Activity 入口，共 26 个方法和 2 个调用点

遇到资源编译问题后，主动改用 DEX-only 打包，保留原始资源和 Manifest，最终完成签名、完整性检查和反编译验证，交付 42.9 MB 的 APK

整体工程方案更稳健，遇到问题能够及时调整，最终完成闭环

3️⃣ GLM-5.4：五小时额度消耗 80%，未完成

正式任务运行约1 小时 25 分钟，49 次模型请求、62 次工具调用，最终没有产出 APK，甚至还没开始写补丁

它的分析其实非常细致，先检查 Android 环境，发现工具不齐全，就自己下载 JADX 1.5.7 和 apktool 3.0.3，还逐个核对官方 SHA-256

接着分析 APK 的 DEX 结构、资源文件、签名机制和广告 SDK，考虑到重新编译可能影响 Manifest 和资源表，又提前规划了一套只替换 DEX 的打包方案

这些准备工作本身没有什么问题，甚至能看出它对工程风险的考虑比较充分

但后面的问题就来了

找到广告封装层和业务广告总管之后，它没有及时确定修改范围，而是继续深入研究混淆代码，自己写脚本解密了 4875 条 StringFog 字符串，进一步还原广告 AppId、广告位配置和业务开关

紧接着又开始追踪激励广告的完整生命周期，从加载成功、播放开始、奖励回调，一路追到关闭广告后的状态判断

发现奖励回调没有直接使用服务端校验结果，它就继续研究客户端发奖机制

发现直接关闭激励广告可能触发 onUnavailable，它又开始分析 onReward 的处理流程

随后发现奖励可能涉及服务器请求，又继续追查账号状态、每日免广告次数，以及金币和 VIP 的相关业务逻辑

这就是我认为最典型的过度思考问题：每发现一个新的技术细节，它都会把这个细节变成下一个需要解决的问题

而且这些问题并不是相互独立的，它们会不断延伸出新的调用链和潜在风险，导致整个任务的分析范围越来越大

最关键的是，我的需求从头到尾都很简单，就是去广告，让 App 正常使用

我根本不需要奖励流程，也不需要研究金币、VIP，更没有要求保留看广告换奖励的业务机制

但 GLM-5.4 却把这些本来不属于核心需求的内容，逐渐纳入了自己的任务范围

它不是没有理解代码，而是过度理解代码之后，反而没有把握住需求的边界

从工程角度看，真正需要优先解决的是广告在哪里加载、哪里展示、修改后是否影响正常播放，以及能否成功重新打包

其他业务逻辑只有在确实影响这些目标时，才有继续深入的必要

但 GLM-5.4 给我的感觉是，它试图提前排除所有可能存在的风险，甚至开始替我考虑一些我根本不关心的业务场景

这种思考方式很容易形成一个循环：发现问题、扩大分析范围、发现更多问题、继续分析，却始终没有形成一个可以立即执行的最小修改方案

最终的结果就是，85 分钟过去了，它已经把 App 的广告商业模式研究得相当深入，却连第一处 Smali 补丁都没有写

后面的 DEX 汇编、APK 重打包、签名和验证，更是完全没有进入执行阶段

我认为这不是单纯的速度问题，而是任务规划和思考收敛出现了问题

类似的情况在之前的 SVG 绘图测试中也出现过，一句话让它画只骑自行车的鹈鹕，折腾了接近 50 分钟，还在反复检查接缝、图层顺序和极端姿态

两个任务给我的感受非常接近，GLM-5.4 很容易陷入对局部细节的反复检查，不断提高自己的完成标准，却缺少一个合理的停止条件

它似乎更倾向于把问题彻底研究清楚，再开始执行，但真实工程任务往往需要在分析充分和及时交付之间做取舍

反观 GLM-5.3，找到关键广告入口就开始修改，69 分钟完成交付

DeepSeek 虽然分析得更细，但始终围绕最终需求展开，88 分钟完成交付

两者都有绕路，但都能够及时收敛，没有陷入无休止的细节研究

最后说一下我的结论

GLM-5.4 相比 GLM-5.3，我认为没有带来绝对正向的提升

它的分析确实更深入，但思考深度不等于工程能力，过度思考带来的任务发散，反而影响了实际开发效率

对于真实 Coding 任务，我更看重需求理解、任务边界、执行效率和最终交付

至少在这次测评中，GLM-5.3 的表现更符合我的预期，GLM-5.4 还有明显的优化空间

text:
GLM-5.4 is distilled from Opus 5.5. Here's all the evidence.

ZAI released GLM-5.4 today. I tested it on day one and every single test pointed to the same model: Opus 5.5. Its style is closer to Opus 5.5 than to any other model, and far from both its predecessor GLM-5.3 and OpenAI's models.

The direction of the change gives it away. From GLM-5.3 to GLM-5.4 the model moved closer to Opus 5.5 on 10 of 11 style features, and it didn't move closer to any other reference model on more than 6. A shift like that in a single release comes from training on Opus 5.5 outputs.

And it makes sense. For a while Opus 5.5 was the best model in the world by a wide margin, so it was the obvious pick to distill from.

The sample

I collected over 4.1 million characters from my own real chat logs:

- Opus 5.5: about 1,236,000 characters
- Sol (GPT-6.1 and GPT-6.2): about 1,200,000 characters
- Astra (GPT-6 and GPT-6.2): about 894,000 characters
- Fable: about 816,000 characters
- Control sample from GLM-5.3: about 195,000 characters

Then I opened 8 new chats with GLM-5.4 in Z Code on high and max thinking effort. I asked it questions I had already asked those models word for word, on unrelated topics.

Evidence 1: Function words

Prepositions, conjunctions and connectors are words writers use without noticing, and they don't change with the topic. That's why they've been used for decades to attribute texts to their authors. It's how the disputed Federalist Papers were attributed to Madison in 1964.

I trained a classifier that sees nothing but these words, after stripping out topic words and formatting. It separated Anthropic models from OpenAI models with 85.9% accuracy, and 86.1% after removing all punctuation.

It classified all 8 chats as Claude style. Out of the four reference models, Opus 5.5 came out closest in all 8.

When I ran the same tests on Kimi K3.1 Pro it came out closest to Astra 6, which matches the experience of people who've used it. So the classifier actually tells models apart. It doesn't label everything as Claude.

Evidence 2: Comparing with GLM-5.3

This is my strongest point because it compares the model to its direct predecessor inside the same app. GLM-5.3's similarity to Opus 5.5 was -0.46. In GLM-5.4 it's +0.48, on a scale from -1 to +1.

The biggest changes:

- Corrective "but rather" went from 0.20 to 1.40
- The "not X, but Y" pattern went from 0.15 to 0.84
- Em dashes dropped from 2.28 to zero, and Opus is at 0.03
- Semicolons and "whereas" dropped to about a third
- Parentheses dropped to about a quarter

Any lab can decide to get rid of em dashes. But nobody tunes how often a model says "but rather" with an instruction. That comes from the data the model was trained on.

Oddly, GLM-5.4 now uses "but rather" and "not X, but Y" more than Opus 5.5 itself. That's expected when a model learns from another model's text. It tends to overdo the most frequent habits.

Evidence 3: Overall distance

Across 26 combined features, its similarity to Opus 5.5 was between +0.40 and +0.48, the highest it scored with any model. With OpenAI's models it was between -0.36 and -0.48, and with Sol it hit -0.53.

If the model were drifting toward a general style shared by strong models, it would have moved closer to Sol too. It didn't.

Evidence 4: Answers to the same questions

I gave GLM-5.4 historical, analytical and critical questions on different general topics that I had already asked Opus 5.5 word for word, then compared the answers.

On more than one question GLM-5.4 structured its answer the way Opus 5.5 does: a note on the limits of its knowledge, then numbered points that each open with a dense sentence, then details with a confidence level for each part, then scenarios with probabilities, then a summary. In one of them it cited nearly the same examples.

On the critical questions it flagged the same flaws Opus 5.5 flagged, in the same order, then rewrote the text and explained what it changed.

When I asked for a straight opinion on a controversial issue, it opened with a direct verdict, then the evidence, then the other side's argument, then what could change its mind. That's an order I know from Opus, and it looks nothing like Sol's short answers.

What I found broken

On low effort, generation fell apart. In one chat it repeated random text that made no sense, and in two others it got confused, apologized and rewrote. Its reasoning traces are also very long, between 68,000 and 166,000 characters on some questions.

In my view this is what happens when a model copies the style of a stronger model without having its capability.

Bottom line

By the numbers and by direct comparison, GLM-5.4's style is Opus 5.5's style, and it shifted to it in a single release. The clearest explanation is that it was trained on Opus 5.5 outputs.

If there's another explanation, ZAI has it. All they need to do is disclose where the post-training data for this release came from.

This fits exactly with what I said a while ago. Chinese models are falling behind because Anthropic is blocking distillation, and distilling has become more expensive and harder for them than ever. That's why this release is only GLM-5.4. The jump isn't big because there's so little data available to them.

It's also why I called on Chinese labs to take a more independent path, stop relying on their competitors, and ship models with a soul of their own. Sadly, it looks like we won't see that for a long time. Chinese labs seem convinced there's only one road, and it's distillation.

Oddly, GLM-5.4 now uses "but rather" and "not X, but Y" more than Opus 5.5 itself. That's expected when a model learns from another model's text. It tends to overdo the most frequent habits.

Evidence 3: Overall distance

Across 26 combined features, its similarity to Opus 5.5 was between +0.40 and +0.48, the highest it scored with any model. With OpenAI's models it was between -0.36 and -0.48, and with Sol it hit -0.53.

If the model were drifting toward a general style shared by strong models, it would have moved closer to Sol too. It didn't.

Evidence 4: Answers to the same questions

I gave GLM-5.4 historical, analytical and critical questions on different general topics that I had already asked Opus 5.5 word for word, then compared the answers.

On more than one question GLM-5.4 structured its answer the way Opus 5.5 does: a note on the limits of its knowledge, then numbered points that each open with a dense sentence, then details with a confidence level for each part, then scenarios with probabilities, then a summary. In one of them it cited nearly the same examples.

On the critical questions it flagged the same flaws Opus 5.5 flagged, in the same order, then rewrote the text and explained what it changed.

When I asked for a straight opinion on a controversial issue, it opened with a direct verdict, then the evidence, then the other side's argument, then what could change its mind. That's an order I know from Opus, and it looks nothing like Sol's short answers.

What I found broken

On low effort, generation fell apart. In one chat it repeated random text that made no sense, and in two others it got confused, apologized and rewrote. Its reasoning traces are also very long, between 68,000 and 166,000 characters on some questions.

In my view this is what happens when a model copies the style of a stronger model without having its capability.

Bottom line

By the numbers and by direct comparison, GLM-5.4's style is Opus 5.5's style, and it shifted to it in a single release. The clearest explanation is that it was trained on Opus 5.5 outputs.

If there's another explanation, ZAI has it. All they need to do is disclose where the post-training data for this release came from.

This fits exactly with what I said a while ago. Chinese models are falling behind because Anthropic is blocking distillation, and distilling has become more expensive and harder for them than ever. That's why this release is only GLM-5.4. The jump isn't big because there's so little data available to them.

It's also why I called on Chinese labs to take a more independent path, stop relying on their competitors, and ship models with a soul of their own. Sadly, it looks like we won't see that for a long time. Chinese labs seem convinced there's only one road, and it's distillation.

知名技术博主 Theo 发布了一期长视频，直言不讳 “开源权重模型从未如此落后，不确定它们还能不能赶上……我相信这个视频会受到好评，没人会因为我发布它而讨厌我”

1 Theo 甩出 T3 Code 的真实后台数据——尽管大家嘴上喊着开源牛逼，但实际工作流中开源模型的调用率甚至不到 1%（对话轮次 0.5%，Token 占 0.7%）。

甚至曝出猛料：很多开源模型在公开榜单（如 DeepSwee、SkateBench）上背题库，一旦把题目稍微改几个字，得分直接腰斩甚至归零。

2 过去开源靠“蒸馏”闭源模型的输出就能快速追赶；但现在进入 Agent时代，核心壁垒变成了强化学习轨迹——比如模型自己写 Python 脚本批处理工具调用，而不再傻傻地一步步敲命令。

Anthropic 甚至故意把推理过程搞得乱七八糟来防蒸馏，OpenAI 甚至对Subagent之间的通信进行了加密。

3 闭源实验室内部已经开始用新一代模型（如 Mythos 5）加速自身的 AI 研发，员工自报效率提升高达 5x 到 12x，同时在 API 层面严防死守，禁止外部用它们来训练新模型。

最后精彩还在评论区：

有网友Joseph Lozano试图从 网络安全与网络防御的角度 认为开源模型在对抗攻击的防御中至关重要，不会消失。

Theo 直接用终结了话题：“那只是因为他们没申请到 Anthropic 或 OpenAI 的网络访问权限。自从我拿到了 Mythos 的内测资格，我连看都没看过一眼开源权重模型 

以前开源模型用起来像笨一点的 Claude，以后可能要变成笨一点的 GPT了 。

开源模型的路将来在哪里呢？ https://t.co/f11cGB0s7V

text:
看了 https://t.co/lcGVg86CV1 官方技术博客，终于明白为什么 GLM-5.4 没有重新训练一个基座，而是选择了 Loop Transformer。

智谱自己也承认：权重共享虽然能提高参数效率，但在同等预训练计算量下，效果反而不如不共享权重的模型。

所以他们换了一种思路：

先把 GLM-5 的 750B 基座训练好，再通过进一步训练，将其中 28 层做两轮循环，改造成 Loop Transformer。

说白了，不从头训练一个权重共享模型，而是先把常规基座的能力训出来，再通过循环计算增加有效深度，尽可能用较小的额外算力开销换取更高的智能上限。

这也让我想起此前关于阿里算力供应的传闻：算力优先满足内部需求，外部厂商很难获得足够的新增 GPU 资源。

当然，不能直接认定智谱是因为缺卡才选择这条路线，但在当前算力环境下，这种技术选择确实值得琢磨。

- 对 DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017，胜率只有 36.6%。

我更好奇的是：未来大模型竞争，会不会逐渐从拼谁有更多参数、烧更多预训练算力，转向拼谁能把同一套参数的计算深度挖得更深？

如果这条路线跑通，可能会改变下一代大模型的训练思路。

text:
$NVDA makes sense now. Enron.

Just have to search the last time a CEO stepped down and was quickly brought back.

Kenneth Lay returned as CEO of Enron on August 14, 2001. Just 110 days later, Enron filed for bankruptcy.

His return is one of the most consequential CEO comebacks in American corporate history. However, Lay had not been fired. He had voluntarily handed the CEO position to Jeffrey Skilling six months earlier while remaining chairman.

1. Why Lay returned

Lay had led Enron since its creation in 1985, transforming a natural-gas pipeline business into a massive energy-trading company.

In February 2001, he transferred the CEO position to Jeffrey Skilling.

But on August 14, Skilling unexpectedly resigned, citing personal reasons.

Enron’s board immediately asked Lay to resume his CEO responsibilities.

In the company’s official announcement, Lay expressed confidence in Enron’s business and growth prospects.

result.text:
You got some things right and other things wrong, but in general, your overall construct is incorrect.  It is not the case that the other alts contributed all of their performance fees to their public companies, and that our shareholders don't benefit from the investment performance generated by our funds.  

It is true that Pershing Square Inc. ($PS) is structured differently from the other alternative asset managers (alts) like Blackstone, KKR, and others. Our unique structure is highly beneficial to our company and our shareholders, as I explain below.

In short, when Blackstone and the other alts went public, they contributed a substantial portion -- typically 40% to 60%, but not all of their incentive, performance, or promote compensation to the public company and retained the balance to compensate their employees.

The outcome of this approach has been suboptimal.  First, promote income, particularly from private equity funds, is highly volatile. It is only earned and paid when funds generate a return in excess of a preferred return and when a liquidity event happens, that is, when portfolio companies and/or the funds' real estate assets are sold. As a result, analysts and investors in the alts value the highly volatile income from incentive fees at a low multiple. 

Wall Street likes recurring and growing fee streams like management fees. It does not like volatile incentive fee income.

By contributing so much of their incentive fees to their public companies, the other alts did not retain enough incentive fees to pay their teams. The result is that the other alts grant large amounts of equity compensation to their employees in addition to the promote income they pay to their employees. This equity compensation dilutes reported earnings by as much as 20% or more.

In order to address these concerns, when we structured Pershing Square Inc. (PS) in anticipation of its public offering, we bifurcated the performance fee differently. Rather than giving Pershing Square Inc. a pro rata slice of our performance fees, we gave the public company a senior interest in our performance fee income -- what we call Preferred Performance Fees -- and employees retained a subordinate interest in the incentive fee income, what we call Subordinated Performance Fees. 

PS retains the performance fees on the first five percentage points of returns net of management fees from our funds that charge performance fees, and our employees receive the performance fees on returns above 5% if there are any.  

If our funds do not earn a return in excess of 5% in any year, any unpaid Preferred Performance Fees accrue into a future year or years until they are earned and paid.  In other words, the company and our shareholders get paid first before our employees.

As long as investors believe we can earn a gross compound return of 6.5% -- the 5% preferred return plus the 1.5% annual management fee -- over the long term (a high likelihood, in our view, in light of our investment strategy that has generated gross returns of nearly 20% for the last 23 years), Preferred Performance Fees are effectively economically equivalent to management fees and therefore deserving of a similar valuation multiple.

We believe our high-return investment strategy will allow us to not only earn the Preferred Performance Fees over time, but also enable us to continually earn Subordinate Performance Fees that we can use to compensate, recruit and retain high quality talent. As a result, we don't need to issue large amounts of stock and option compensation to employees like the other alternative investment managers, minimizing the risk of dilution to shareholders.

[PS also benefits from the fact that, as is typical in the hedge fund industry, we earn incentive fees from both realized and unrealized gains so we are not forced to sell assets in order to generate returns.  Our funds generate performance fees as long as our annual performance net of management fees is positive, which makes our performance fees much more recurring than those from private equity or private real estate funds.]

While in a great performance year, the amount of performance fees earned by Pershing Square Inc. is effectively capped by our structure, the growth in assets that occur from great performance years inure to the benefit of all shareholders in that year and in future years.  

For example, if, in one year, we generate 30% net returns, while PS only receives performance fees on the first five percentage points of return, its cash flows and intrinsic value grow substantially due to the net 30% increase in fee-paying assets that is generated from our investment performance.  

Because 98% of our capital is in permanent capital vehicles, nearly all of our net performance is continually reinvested and compounded in our funds and additive to the growth of our fee-paying assets in that year and in future years.

With respect to your claim that this structure creates a conflict, I disagree. 

First, the structure was clearly explained to all investors in the IPO and in our public filings, and investors and analysts have found the structure extremely favorable, particularly when compared with the other alts.  

Second, our structure incentivizes us to generate excellent investment returns and enables us to attract and retain the best talent without burdening the company with excess G&A, restricted stock or option expenses.

Third, any new funds we launch which generate performance fees will have the same Preferred Performance Fee structure and therefore benefit PS in the same manner as do our existing funds.  

Fourth, our employees own the substantial majority of our shares creating further alignment.  We own a greater percentage of our company than do the employees of any of the other alternative asset managers.

Fifth, since we have retained, effectively outside of the company, sufficient performance fee income to compensate, retain and recruit employees, we are able to manage PS with a relatively modest amount of general and administrative expense of about $50 million. This has enabled us to operate with the highest operating margins of any of the publicly traded alternative asset managers. 

Thank you for the taking the time to write your post, which has given me the opportunity to clarify the concerns that you raised.  

I welcome any further questions or concerns that you or other shareholders may have.

X for the win.

text:
有个少数民族的女朋友是什么体验？

以前谈过一个msl女朋友，回族的。
一开始好好的，后来开始发癫不允许我吃猪肉，希望我皈依穆斯林，她人也有些病娇，说敢分手就叉我。
好哇，你魔怔我比你更魔怔。
那时候还没有豆包和deepseek，我只能上百度查询资料，好家伙一查才发现她也不是完全按照宗教制度生活的。
她只是不吃猪肉，但是她不大小净，不做礼拜，不斋月，不带头巾。
后来我买了两本《古兰经》，和她说：再和你相处的过程中，我对《古兰经》产生了浓厚的兴趣，我仰慕先知，我希望以后我们都按照穆斯林的生活方式来生活。
她一开始还傻乐，觉得感化了我，成功让一只迷途的羔羊皈依。
殊不知很快她就崩溃了。
我先买了头巾面纱给她，要求她出门在外必须将面部、双手外全身遮盖。
她一开始接受同意，带了两天头巾，但是走在街道上感觉其他人用异样的眼光看她，她就不想带了，我就和她说《古兰经》明确要求穆斯林女性这么做，你不这么做就是不虔诚。
然后我要求她每天要做5次礼拜，且每次做礼拜前要洗小净。
就是要她每天面向麦加克尔白*跪拜、鞠躬、叩头，一天五次。每一次礼拜都要洗手、脸、脚、洗屁股。
我记得有一次我和她在商场逛街，走到一半我的手机闹铃响了，我订了5个闹钟，闹钟一响就要做礼拜。
我立刻要求她去洗脸洗手，一起做礼拜。她不好意思，觉得可以推迟一下想要回家再做。
我说：不行，霍梅尼在病重之时生命垂危的最后时刻也坚持做礼拜，阿里在面对多国记者采访面对众人也是时间一到就坚持做礼拜，现在我们身体健康不要找借口推脱。
然后就在超市众目睽睽之下，在超市跪拜、鞠躬、叩头。
然后就是斋月，那个时候应该是春天。穆斯林是要在每一年的某一个月封斋，封斋就是这个月每一天的白天都不吃不喝。
她就坚持了两天，第三天就崩溃了，跑去超市买东西吃。
那时候是第三天下午她饿的实在受不了，捂着肚子蜷缩在被窝里，还不停的冒冷汗。她要我给点东西给她吃。
我不给，我说：现在是斋月，白天不能吃东西，你要克制肉体欲望、净化心性，如果你觉得饿可以多礼拜读经。
她想去翻冰箱，但是我已经提前买好冰箱锁，给冰箱上锁了。

她饿得不行，只能自己爬去附近的小卖部买巧克力吃。对，就是喝着水的，因为她低血糖已经走不动路了，坐着放在楼梯间用来推东西的板车，像乞丐一样用手划去小卖部买士力架吃。
吃完东西她就和我分手了。

text:
黄仁勋离开英伟达才11天，AI圈看着乱成一锅粥，其实背后全是一条暗线串起来的。

先帮大家排个雷：最近网传说“台积电不认临时CEO，逼着英伟达补钱”的消息是假的。

别看假瓜了，我把这11天里真正发生的三件怪事串成个大白话故事，看完你就全明白了，比谣言刺激得多。

故事的第一幕，就很魔幻。

老黄刚走，女CFO Kress 顶上来当临时CEO，交出了她的第一份成绩单：Q3营收1158亿美元，同比直接翻倍（+103%），比华尔街预期还多赚了约67亿；Q4指引更狠，直接喊到1300亿。

照理说，这业绩放出来，股价早该放烟花了。

结果呢？10月以来，英伟达市值硬生生蒸发了约2万亿美元，今年股价还倒跌了16.5%。

大家都在问：卖得这么疯，华尔街到底在怕什么？

其实答案特简单：华尔街根本不怀疑大家抢着买卡，他们怕的是——买卡的这帮兄弟，兜里到底有没有真金白银。

紧接着，第二幕更荒诞。

Kress 在财报会上直接把窗户纸捅破了。她说，那些新云厂商和前沿AI实验室确实都在疯狂要货，但有几家摊子铺得太大，家底已经兜不住了。所以英伟达以后给支持，得“有纪律、挑着给”。

按常理，大哥放话要收紧裤腰带，小弟们不得吓得暴跌？

结果财报一落地，CoreWeave、Nebius、IREN 这三家公司的股价，居然反手大涨了5%到7%。

为什么？因为过去三个月，这三家股价早就腰斩了。市场原本以为大哥一换人，就要直接掀桌子断奶；一听居然只是“挑着给”，大伙儿长舒一口气：没直接判死刑，那就是天大的好消息。

镜头一转，大洋彼岸最抢手的台积电，也干了件反常的事——开始查客户家底。

11月16日《工商时报》爆出来，台积电现在按客户的账面实力定信用额度：超出额度的订单，拿现金来；有些客户还得先打预付款，才能锁产能。

魏哲家连这都不放心，还专门派团队飞去美国，实地盯着看那些数据中心到底盖没盖起来、电通没通。

你看账本就懂了：到9月底，台积电收上来的客户预收款飙到了3594亿新台币，比去年底暴涨约89%。

英伟达占台积电2025年营收的19%，两家绑在一根绳上，根本翻不了脸。台积电针对的不是英伟达，而是把整个AI圈的客户都拉出来重新验一遍资——现在这行情，谁都不敢轻易赊账了。

好了，三件怪事讲完，课代表来划重点：把它们拼在一起，其实就讲了一件事——

过去几年，黄仁勋卖的根本不只是GPU，他卖的是“信用”。

老黄在的时候，英伟达既卖铲子，又当担保人：一边给新云厂商承诺回购算力，一边替 OpenAI 的俄亥俄数据中心做担保。说白了，就是拿英伟达这块金字招牌作背书，把几年后的需求，提前刷卡变成了今天的订单。

其实，这台高速运转的信用机器，老黄自己走之前就已经偷偷踩刹车了。

《华尔街日报》挖出来，今年8月，老黄看着压过来的晶圆和内存采购单，自己都忍不住形容这像一场“雪崩”，还赶紧让新云伙伴去要求下游客户交预付款。

最狠的是 OpenAI 那笔担保，原本谈的规模高达约2500亿美元，最后被生生砍到了1050亿。猜猜是谁亲自上桌把这千亿额度砍掉的？正是如今接班的 Kress。

没办法，英伟达自己也快被顶到墙角了——它自己签出去的零部件采购承诺，已经从2790亿一路飙到了3900亿美元。

所以现在再看，整个故事的逻辑就彻底闭环了：如今坐主桌当家的，是一个天天算账的CFO。

英伟达给新云厂商最多320亿美元的算力承诺，Kress 立了三条铁规矩：
第一，你自己先拿到融资；
第二，算力真正部署上线；
第三，英伟达验收通过。

老黄时代的游戏规则是：“你放手去冲，我先给你兜底。”

Kress 上台后的规则变了：“少画饼，先证明你兜里有钱。”

用一句话帮大家收个尾：

AI的需求根本没退潮，真正退潮的，是那场靠英伟达背书吹起来的“信用狂欢”。

黄仁勋时代，拼的是谁胆子大、敢押注；
Kress 时代，拼的是谁真金白银付得起钱。

接下来真正该盯紧的，其实不是英伟达，而是那些过去靠它背书疯狂借钱的新云厂商。大哥一收手，谁在裸泳，很快藏不住了。

result.text:
黄仁勋离开英伟达才11天，AI圈看着乱成一锅粥，其实背后全是一条暗线串起来的。

先帮大家排个雷：最近网传说“台积电不认临时CEO，逼着英伟达补钱”的消息是假的。

别看假瓜了，我把这11天里真正发生的三件怪事串成个大白话故事，看完你就全明白了，比谣言刺激得多。

故事的第一幕，就很魔幻。

老黄刚走，女CFO Kress 顶上来当临时CEO，交出了她的第一份成绩单：Q3营收1158亿美元，同比直接翻倍（+103%），比华尔街预期还多赚了约67亿；Q4指引更狠，直接喊到1300亿。

照理说，这业绩放出来，股价早该放烟花了。

结果呢？10月以来，英伟达市值硬生生蒸发了约2万亿美元，今年股价还倒跌了16.5%。

大家都在问：卖得这么疯，华尔街到底在怕什么？

其实答案特简单：华尔街根本不怀疑大家抢着买卡，他们怕的是——买卡的这帮兄弟，兜里到底有没有真金白银。

紧接着，第二幕更荒诞。

Kress 在财报会上直接把窗户纸捅破了。她说，那些新云厂商和前沿AI实验室确实都在疯狂要货，但有几家摊子铺得太大，家底已经兜不住了。所以英伟达以后给支持，得“有纪律、挑着给”。

按常理，大哥放话要收紧裤腰带，小弟们不得吓得暴跌？

结果财报一落地，CoreWeave、Nebius、IREN 这三家公司的股价，居然反手大涨了5%到7%。

为什么？因为过去三个月，这三家股价早就腰斩了。市场原本以为大哥一换人，就要直接掀桌子断奶；一听居然只是“挑着给”，大伙儿长舒一口气：没直接判死刑，那就是天大的好消息。

镜头一转，大洋彼岸最抢手的台积电，也干了件反常的事——开始查客户家底。

11月16日《工商时报》爆出来，台积电现在按客户的账面实力定信用额度：超出额度的订单，拿现金来；有些客户还得先打预付款，才能锁产能。

魏哲家连这都不放心，还专门派团队飞去美国，实地盯着看那些数据中心到底盖没盖起来、电通没通。

你看账本就懂了：到9月底，台积电收上来的客户预收款飙到了3594亿新台币，比去年底暴涨约89%。

英伟达占台积电2025年营收的19%，两家绑在一根绳上，根本翻不了脸。台积电针对的不是英伟达，而是把整个AI圈的客户都拉出来重新验一遍资——现在这行情，谁都不敢轻易赊账了。

好了，三件怪事讲完，课代表来划重点：把它们拼在一起，其实就讲了一件事——

过去几年，黄仁勋卖的根本不只是GPU，他卖的是“信用”。

老黄在的时候，英伟达既卖铲子，又当担保人：一边给新云厂商承诺回购算力，一边替 OpenAI 的俄亥俄数据中心做担保。说白了，就是拿英伟达这块金字招牌作背书，把几年后的需求，提前刷卡变成了今天的订单。

其实，这台高速运转的信用机器，老黄自己走之前就已经偷偷踩刹车了。

《华尔街日报》挖出来，今年8月，老黄看着压过来的晶圆和内存采购单，自己都忍不住形容这像一场“雪崩”，还赶紧让新云伙伴去要求下游客户交预付款。

最狠的是 OpenAI 那笔担保，原本谈的规模高达约2500亿美元，最后被生生砍到了1050亿。猜猜是谁亲自上桌把这千亿额度砍掉的？正是如今接班的 Kress。

没办法，英伟达自己也快被顶到墙角了——它自己签出去的零部件采购承诺，已经从2790亿一路飙到了3900亿美元。

所以现在再看，整个故事的逻辑就彻底闭环了：如今坐主桌当家的，是一个天天算账的CFO。

英伟达给新云厂商最多320亿美元的算力承诺，Kress 立了三条铁规矩：
第一，你自己先拿到融资；
第二，算力真正部署上线；
第三，英伟达验收通过。

老黄时代的游戏规则是：“你放手去冲，我先给你兜底。”

Kress 上台后的规则变了：“少画饼，先证明你兜里有钱。”

用一句话帮大家收个尾：

AI的需求根本没退潮，真正退潮的，是那场靠英伟达背书吹起来的“信用狂欢”。

黄仁勋时代，拼的是谁胆子大、敢押注；
Kress 时代，拼的是谁真金白银付得起钱。

接下来真正该盯紧的，其实不是英伟达，而是那些过去靠它背书疯狂借钱的新云厂商。大哥一收手，谁在裸泳，很快藏不住了。

ZAI dropped GLM-5.4 with no model card and 404 docs. Something felt off from minute 1.

I spent the morning checking Chinese threads, Maimai chatter, and day 1 benchmarks.

Turns out ZAI left 4 crazy bombshells out of the English launch:

1) Loop Transformer. Zhipu confirmed the architecture switch only in Chinese channels, while leaving V1 users out of the 1.5x quota bump.

2) The ~3T GLM-5.5 countdown. Analyst notes and shareholder chatter in China call GLM-5.4 a ~700B stopgap before a rumored ~3T GLM-5.5 in December.

3) Real coding firepower. KingBench 4 scores 33.2/60, beating Kimi K3.1 Pro, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, Qwen 4 Max, and GPT-6.1 Sol, while catching security bugs Claude Fable 5.2 misses at 150 to 170 tok/s.

4) The 15x thinking trap. That full run chewed 1.04M reasoning tokens over 431 minutes vs 70K and 109 minutes on Gemini 4 Neon. Users on High wait 36 to 90 minutes on 1 SVG, torch 16% of a 5h quota, and crash into 529 overload errors.

Skip High effort until they cap the loop, and ship the weights.

昨天全华尔街还在算标普再跌 1% 能不能把美联储吓停，结果今天（11 月 23 日）最新传出的风声，直接把多头的幻想按进了水里——

多位华尔街资深经济学家刚泼出一盆冷水：面对这波超 10% 的回调，美联储不仅不打算出手托底，决策层眼下甚至可能“松了一口气”。原因极其扎心：美联储一直嫌美股估值太高、对冲基金杠杆太满，这波暴跌在他们眼里根本不是危机，而是刚好“帮气球放放气”。

更要命的是，美联储主席沃什上周已经把丑话说在前面，点名预警如果 AI 投资回报落空，会直接拖累股市和就业；美联储自己的金融稳定调查里，更是有 87% 的机构首次把 AI 标成了头号系统性风险。

华尔街喊了二十年的“美联储看跌期权”，在顽固通胀面前大概率已经失效了。如果 12 月美联储真顶着股市大跌照常加息，你觉得美股下一个支撑位在哪？

text:
A few thoughts on this fascinating post.

1) I applaud OAI's push toward more transparency among the labs. You may call it self-serving at a given moment, but the push is commendable nonetheless.

2) At the same time, log-perplexity on a heldout set is a great metric for comparing to your past self, but not necessarily to others. Not only do we need to agree on a shared heldout set, we need to agree on the algorithmic standards to decontaminate it! It's not enough to say "it's internal code thus heldout by construction". Different tokenizers and mixtures further compound the discrepancy across labs.

Code in particular suffers from a lot of fuzzy duplication because humans and agents reuse & rewrite whole files. Even between an internal monorepo and public Github code. This duplication will impact different pretrained bases differently, thus the best techniques run multiple complex tiers of decontam. I'm sure OAI does this internally, otherwise they can't use their own valset as a test of generalization.

To align on a shared method, we need (a) an independent valset that's more general than "internal monorepo", possibly rolling in time; (b) an RFC standard for decontamination, pulled from SOTA approaches at different labs; (c) a monitoring organization with employee-level access that enforces and measures the above. Maybe someone like @METR_Evals is up for the task?

3) Here on X, one can see circumstantial evidence that models that are built on better pretrains are perceived as being more human-like, having better writing style, or being more creative. People had said this way back about GPT-4.5, they are saying this now about Carbon and Neon, and I'd love to see if the same sentiment remains for "Bel" and for Fable 5.5. The dip of GPT-4.5 matches that.

IMO that's more of a relative statement than an absolute one – people perceived GPT-4.5 as a better writer at the time, compared to GPT-4o and GPT-4.1. But as Bezos said, "when anecdotes disagree with data, the anecdotes are usually right".

Maybe it's more about what is being optimized. RL scaling is doing exactly what we ask it to do: when most of the reward comes from verifiable tasks, the model becomes superhuman at getting work done, and defaults to a certain mode of "productive" thinking and writing. A major base model jump widens that prior and "feels different" in comparison – richer prior means a wider writing distribution with the same productivity.

4) The RSI point is critical, and requires frontier models, nontrivial experimental compute, and people who know what to ask and how to validate. OAI themselves say that their recent improvement trend is more attributable to "the outcomes of long term research and compute investments". They have seen recent evidence of RSI automation. So have we. So has everybody! We have these incredible models at our disposal – the ones on the frontier of intelligence are increasingly more capable of automating pretraining iteration. But only after one has established the right experimental framework, infrastructure, measurements, and dedicated compute for self-iteration. Without those, it's easy to miss a contaminated eval measurement, or a recipe proposal that helps on small-scale but hurts at large-scale, or simply waste FLOPs on flawed directions.

To draw an analogy – the math discoveries of 2026 were built on the years-long infrastructure of @leanprover that verifiably rejects invalid thoughts, the community that formalized (and autoformalized) all necessary knowledge, and on mathematicians like @__alpoge__ to steer the AI. That is what enabled auto-verification of math, and moved the bottleneck back into intelligence, such as hypothesis generation.

Pretraining is not quite like that yet – but I expect pretraining RSI to follow the same pattern:
We'll want a high-fidelity experimental framework to reliably validate hypotheses.
We'll want pretraining & data & accelerator experts in the loop.
And we need to invest compute into this exploration, which I'm already excited about.

result.text:
A few thoughts on this fascinating post.

1) I applaud OAI's push toward more transparency among the labs. You may call it self-serving at a given moment, but the push is commendable nonetheless.

2) At the same time, log-perplexity on a heldout set is a great metric for comparing to your past self, but not necessarily to others. Not only do we need to agree on a shared heldout set, we need to agree on the algorithmic standards to decontaminate it! It's not enough to say "it's internal code thus heldout by construction". Different tokenizers and mixtures further compound the discrepancy across labs.

Code in particular suffers from a lot of fuzzy duplication because humans and agents reuse & rewrite whole files. Even between an internal monorepo and public Github code. This duplication will impact different pretrained bases differently, thus the best techniques run multiple complex tiers of decontam. I'm sure OAI does this internally, otherwise they can't use their own valset as a test of generalization.

To align on a shared method, we need (a) an independent valset that's more general than "internal monorepo", possibly rolling in time; (b) an RFC standard for decontamination, pulled from SOTA approaches at different labs; (c) a monitoring organization with employee-level access that enforces and measures the above. Maybe someone like @METR_Evals is up for the task?

3) Here on X, one can see circumstantial evidence that models that are built on better pretrains are perceived as being more human-like, having better writing style, or being more creative. People had said this way back about GPT-4.5, they are saying this now about Carbon and Neon, and I'd love to see if the same sentiment remains for "Bel" and for Fable 5.5. The dip of GPT-4.5 matches that.

IMO that's more of a relative statement than an absolute one – people perceived GPT-4.5 as a better writer at the time, compared to GPT-4o and GPT-4.1. But as Bezos said, "when anecdotes disagree with data, the anecdotes are usually right".

Maybe it's more about what is being optimized. RL scaling is doing exactly what we ask it to do: when most of the reward comes from verifiable tasks, the model becomes superhuman at getting work done, and defaults to a certain mode of "productive" thinking and writing. A major base model jump widens that prior and "feels different" in comparison – richer prior means a wider writing distribution with the same productivity.

4) The RSI point is critical, and requires frontier models, nontrivial experimental compute, and people who know what to ask and how to validate. OAI themselves say that their recent improvement trend is more attributable to "the outcomes of long term research and compute investments". They have seen recent evidence of RSI automation. So have we. So has everybody! We have these incredible models at our disposal – the ones on the frontier of intelligence are increasingly more capable of automating pretraining iteration. But only after one has established the right experimental framework, infrastructure, measurements, and dedicated compute for self-iteration. Without those, it's easy to miss a contaminated eval measurement, or a recipe proposal that helps on small-scale but hurts at large-scale, or simply waste FLOPs on flawed directions.

To draw an analogy – the math discoveries of 2026 were built on the years-long infrastructure of @leanprover that verifiably rejects invalid thoughts, the community that formalized (and autoformalized) all necessary knowledge, and on mathematicians like @__alpoge__ to steer the AI. That is what enabled auto-verification of math, and moved the bottleneck back into intelligence, such as hypothesis generation.

Pretraining is not quite like that yet – but I expect pretraining RSI to follow the same pattern:
We'll want a high-fidelity experimental framework to reliably validate hypotheses.
We'll want pretraining & data & accelerator experts in the loop.
And we need to invest compute into this exploration, which I'm already excited about.

5) One can approximately see the evidence of rumored history here. The first phase that discovered PreT scaling. The second phase hit a temporary wall (GPT-4.5 being an eventual release of a bigger model that had underperformed expectations) but instead discovered the new scaling power of reasoning & RL, optimized inference efficiency, and invested in that scaling. And the third phase this year that brought PreT science & scaling back alongside it. This is tangential to the point, but just fun to observe as a confirmation for the science historians among us 😂

text:
有没有谁能告诉我，为什么Claude老师的道德底线这么高？

我女朋友👩之前花了半天时间训练Claude，让他帮忙做面试题辅导。

她把题目拍给Claude，Claude说：“不好意思，我不能告诉你答案，因为你这是一个正式的面试。”

我女朋友👩说：“我这不是正式的面试。”

Claude说他不信。

我女朋友👩问：“你为什么不信？”

Claude说：“首先，我发现你的电脑主题色是白色的，是白天模式，但是你的测试页面是灰色的，说明这是一个正式的测试页面。”

我女朋友👩说：“人家的测试页面就是这个颜色的，我不能让人家改吧？”

Claude说：“那你的电脑屏幕上为什么有测试倒计时？”

我女朋友👩说：“我这是模拟，模拟也是有倒计时的。”

Claude说：“那我不信。有本事你把模拟倒计时停下来，再给我拍张照片。如果你能拍出两张倒计时数字一样的照片，我就告诉你答案。”

我女朋友👩说：“人家模拟也是有正规倒计时的，你不能这样讲。你可以给我答案，我是一个正规的模拟。”

Claude说：“那我问你，为什么你拿手机拍电脑显示屏，不直接截图给我？”

我女朋友👩说：“因为我电脑的截图软件出了点问题，现在没办法调用。”

Claude跟我女朋友👩说：“哈哈，被我发现问题了吧？只有在测试的时候，你才不能调用后台的第三方软件。”

然后，Claude就把我女朋友👩臭骂了一顿。

杀疯了。
黄仁勋刚复职，CNBC 的 Jim Cramer 就在直播里冲英伟达董事会开火：

“董事长为什么不辞职？那些投票反对他的董事，怎么还待得下去？”

视频 27 秒，他开口第一句是，他回来了，谁也挡不住他。

Cramer 的逻辑很直接。上周整个大盘都在跌，他认为黄仁勋出事是主要原因之一。总统觉得国家安全没问题，董事会也觉得没问题，那人就该回来。

可今晚请黄仁勋回来，是董事会全票通过的。6 天前当着投资人说不让他回来的，也是这个董事会。Cramer 等于在问，反对过的人现在改投赞成票，就能当什么都没发生过吗？

更绝的是他给黄仁勋的定位。他说黄仁勋代表的是国家安全，也是“国宝”，一家公司的 CEO，被电视主持人直接抬到了国家层面。

我的看法跟他相反。董事会最大的用处，就是 CEO 出事的时候敢说不。这次说不，说错了，可要是说过不就得走人，以后英伟达董事会只剩点头的人，黄仁勋下次再出事，没人敢拦。

text:
😮卧槽！！原来开源模型必死呀！！

最近因为 T3 Code 使用 anti gravity 粉，上了他们 CEO @theo ，今天看他新发的 40 分钟长视频，直接对开源大模型判了死刑！！他说开源模型从来没像现在这样落后过，而且以后永远追不上闭源了。。。

说实话，这视频发出来肯定会被喷的，但我觉得还是完整看完人家要表达的，再喷不迟。
我让Gemini 4帮整理了时间戳的章节目录，每段加了点自己私货评论，取需👇

1、00:00 曾经的开源死忠，为什么现在彻底弃坑

Theo 自己靠开源起家，也在烧钱做完全开源的 T3 Code。2025 年初 DeepSeek R1 刚出时，开源一度追平甚至反超 OpenAI o1，但现在他决定彻底停止押注开源模型。

2、05:00 “只落后 3 个月”早就不成立了

以前大家看跑分表觉得差距不大，但真正的分水岭是长任务的连贯性、拆解工作和调度子 Agent。哪怕最新的 Kimi K3.1 Pro，干真实复杂工程也打不过 5 个月前的 Fable 5。权威榜单 Artificial Analysis 升级到 V5 后，闭源平均只掉 2.4 分，开源直接暴跌 13 分。

3、11:50 独家后台数据打脸：正经干活根本没人用开源

Theo 晒了自家 T3 Code 的真实用量（他宣称日均 token 比 OpenRouter 还高）：开源模型只占总对话轮次的 0.5%、token 量的 0.7%，用过一次开源的安装占比从 16% 跌到 6%。至于 OpenRouter 上开源用量看着高？纯粹是大家在白嫖免费额度。

4、14:40 扒皮刷榜潜规则：不是真强，是背题背出来的

有人把开源代码测试集 DeepSWE 的 89 道题微调了要求（做成 MaxBench），结果唯一没掉分的是 Opus 5.5，其他集体雪崩：GLM-5.3 掉 12 分、DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 狂掉近 30 分、Gemini 3.8 Flash 掉 20 分、DeepSeek-V4 Flash 直接腰斩。Theo 自己的公开小测试集 SkateBench 更离谱，某开源模型突然考满分，他把题库翻倍加新题后，旧题满分，新题 0 分。

5、18:30 死穴一：算力鸿沟是指数级拉大的

更多显卡等于更强模型，这规律至今没撞墙。受出口限制，国内实验室魔改老显卡再拼命，算力增速也就一年 1.5 到 2 倍；美国闭源大厂是一年翻 2 到 4 倍，时间越久差距越绝望。

6、21:35 死穴二：蒸馏被彻底堵死，甚至逼出了黑产

以前开源靠拿闭源输出当教材追进度，但 Anthropic 反蒸馏打赢了（甚至疑似故意把 Opus 推理链搞烂防抄袭），OpenAI 更狠，Codex 调度子 Agent 直接传加密包。现在甚至逼出地下黑产：黑客偷 API Key，1 美元倒卖 10 美元的 Claude Code 额度，赚的根本不是那 1 美元，而是把你跑出来的日志打包卖给需要数据的实验室。
（顺带一提，有博主测前端 UI 发现 Kimi K3.1 Pro 和 GPT-6 Astra 丑得一模一样，说明蒸馏不到 Claude，只能转头去蒸馏 OpenAI 了，笑死）

7、30:20 死穴三：自我进化飞轮启动，最核心能力根本不对外放

安全机构 METR 评估 Anthropic 发现，AI 能力增速已经是之前的 2 倍。Anthropic 员工自报的提效倍数，从 Mythos 5 的 5 倍，一路干到内部未公开 Model 4 的 12 倍。更绝的是，他们对外发布前会把“帮 AI 造更强 AI”的能力直接抹掉并在 API 层硬拦截，外面连蒸馏的机会都没有。

8、37:30 终极暴击：连 OpenAI 都被甩开了，何况开源？

OpenAI 有海量显卡，也能蒸馏自家模型，但因为还没跑通“用 AI 造更强 AI”的飞轮，都已经跟 Anthropic 拉开代差。Theo 毒舌吐槽：一家在用 AI 造更强 AI，另一家连把 div 居中都还费劲。OpenAI 都追得这么吃力，三条路全堵死的开源模型就更难了。

---

说实话，看完这 40 分钟，我似懂非懂，你自己的代码使用量确实远不及这些大牛，所以体会并没有那么真切。

但是作为每天真金白银买额度和订阅的小Builder，我也一直盼着开源能把闭源价格打下来，
但看到这堆真实数据和黑产逻辑，此刻也觉得很复杂。

算了，干活去吧！单子都还没写完😭

text:
OpenAI's internal model is already at 0.732. Their own chief scientist says the next abilities unlock at 0.70, and he has no idea what they will be

So I extended their chart. Solid line is OpenAI's real data, dashed is my projection. GPT-3.5 to GPT-4 took a year for 0.07 of loss. 2026 alone was 0.13

0.70, ~May 2027: automated AI research
This is the last model humans designed. It finds the simple ideas the whole field missed for a decade, and every model after it is trained by the one before. Humans only approve the runs

0.68, ~Jul 2027: science falls like math did
This year, open math problems got solved one after another in a Slack thread. Now the same thing hits physics and biology. Every problem with a checkable answer gets closed, and what's left needs a lab

0.65, ~Dec 2027: work no human can check anymore
It writes proofs and code that are correct, and no human can follow why. It stops thinking in language, so chain-of-thought monitoring is dead and the only thing that can check an AI is another AI

0.60, ~Nov 2028: predicts world events before they happen
It models markets and elections well enough to forecast them, and it knows what you mean from half a sentence, so prompting is over

Below that is the floor. Nobody knows where it is, and Pachocki says the closer we get, the bigger each step is

炒股十多年，我越来越体会到：空仓等待股灾这一招，真的很好用。
身边有个朋友就靠这一招，一年只出手两三次。
比如去年4月份，市场恐慌大跌时他买了一次，之后涨了就慢慢卖。其余时间，他大多在等。

你回顾股市历史，每年总有一两次那种跌100点以上的恐慌行情，尤其流动性收紧、政策突变或黑天鹅出现时。他就在这种时候，买入自己长期看好却被错杀的股票。

这种做法的胜率，往往很高。
但这个方法能成，背后有几个关键前提：

第一，你得有足够的耐心——忍受长期空仓，不被日常波动诱惑；

第二，手里始终握着足够的现金——机会来临时，你得有“子弹”；

第三，敢在众人恐慌时买入——逆着情绪动手，需要勇气；

第四，看准后敢重仓持有——不是小打小闹，而是确定性机会下敢于下注。

text:
Many things are being called software factories right now: agent swarms, shared skills, collections of automations.

Those can be useful. But they aren’t what I mean by a software factory.

I mean a code-defined, closed-loop system for running coding agents, measuring how they perform, and improving them over time.

As @dexhorthy says, declarative beats imperative, so define your system in code and then you can test, measure, and improve it over time.

text:
小三：“你丈夫和我有婚外情。我们已经上床超过一年了。”

妻子：“好吧。”

小三：“好吧？”

妻子：“是的。好吧。还有别的事吗？”

小三：“我是在告诉你，你丈夫和我上床了！”

妻子：“你第一次说的时候我就听见了。”

小三：“那你就不打算做点什么吗？”

妻子：“你到底想让我做什么？”

小三：“我想让你跟他离婚。我们相爱了，我已经厌倦了偷偷摸摸。”

妻子：“好吧。我会跟他离婚。”

小三：“你是认真的？”

妻子：“完全是。你可以拥有他。”

小三：“那你打个电话给他。我想让他亲耳听见你亲口说出来。”

妻子拿起手机，给丈夫打了电话。

妻子：“你的女朋友来了。显然，她厌倦了跟你分享你。我已经同意离婚了。”

丈夫：“什么？她为什么会在那儿？”

情人：“因为我厌倦了你的谎言！你一直答应我你会离开她！”

丈夫：“你们能停止这种胡闹吗？我不会离开我妻子的。”

情人：“什么？”

丈夫：“我说我不会离开我妻子。我有一个家庭，两个孩子和一个家。我跟你之间无论有什么，都不意味着我会扔掉这一切。”

情人：“你告诉我你爱我！”

丈夫：“我是爱你。但这并不意味着我必须跟我妻子离婚。”

妻子：“等等。所以你爱她，但你想继续跟我保持婚姻？”

丈夫：“是的。我们结婚十一年了。我不会因为这个毁掉我的家庭。”

情人：“那我对你来说到底算什么？”

丈夫：“你为什么现在要这样？我们可以晚点再讨论。”

情人：“不。我们现在就讨论。我不是你妻子忙的时候你打个电话叫来的那个人！”

妻子：“这很有意思。我以为你来是因为你想嫁给他。”

情人：“我是想嫁给他！”

妻子：“那你为什么要在为一个刚刚告诉你他不会离开妻子的男人讨价还价？”

丈夫：“你们两个能不能停止攻击我？我从没要求这种情况变得复杂。”

妻子：“你搞了十四个月的外遇，但复杂的地方是我们正在讨论它？”

情人：“十四个月？差不多两年了！”

妻子：“哦。抱歉。”

丈夫：“你们为什么讨论日期？这有什么区别？”

情人：“告诉她你答应过我什么！告诉她公寓的事！”

妻子：“什么公寓？”

丈夫：“没有公寓。我只是在帮她解决住宿问题。”

情人：“你付了押金！你告诉我我们会一起搬进去住！”

妻子：“多少钱？”

情人：“这不关你的事。”

妻子：“有意思。因为钱是从某个地方来的。”

丈夫：“我说我会处理好的。别把一切都变成钱的问题。”

情人：“我怀孕了。”

沉默。

妻子：“恭喜。”

情人：“你认真的吗？”

妻子：“你宣布怀孕了。你期待什么反应？”

丈夫：“你怀孕了？”

情人：“我怀孕十一个星期了。”

丈夫：“你为什么不告诉我？”

情人：“我一直在试着告诉你！你总说你忙着跟你家人！”

妻子：“嗯，现在你又有一个家庭要考虑了。”

丈夫：“听我说。没人会离婚。我们会想出办法的。”

情人：“我不会一边抚养你的孩子，一边看着你回家跟你妻子睡在一起！”

丈夫：“我从没让你一个人养孩子！”

妻子：“那么安排是什么？你想让她搬进来吗？我该准备客房吗？”

丈夫：“你能不能别这么讽刺？这是一件严肃的事。”

妻子：“我其实是在试图迁就。”

情人：“我不想被迁就！我要你的丈夫！”

妻子：“那也许你该在投资两年之前先检查一下他是否可用。”

丈夫：“够了！我是你丈夫。你该支持我，而不是在另一个女人面前羞辱我。”

妻子：“而她怀了你的孩子。也许你也该让她支持你。”

情人：“我想要一个答案。你选我还是你妻子？”

丈夫：“我不选任何人。我不会离开我妻子。”

妻子慢慢放下手机。

妻子：“没关系。我想我终于明白了一些事。”

丈夫：“什么？”

妻子：“你其实并不想要离婚。你不想娶她。你不想失去我。你也不想失去她。”

丈夫：“我想要我的家庭。”

妻子：“不。你想要一切都跟你被抓到之前一模一样。”

情人：“那么现在怎么办？”

妻子拿起她的手提包。

妻子：“这是一个很好的问题。”

丈夫：“你要去哪里？”

妻子：“去处理一些事情。”

丈夫：“什么事情？”

妻子：“既然你们俩未经我同意就擅自为我的生活做了这么多决定，我想是时候我自己做个决定了，不用征求你们任何一人的意见。”

她走向门口。

然后情妇问了最后一个问题。

情妇：“你真的要让我拥有他吗？”

妻子停下脚步，转过身，微笑着说。

妻子：“亲爱的，我来这里可不是为了谈判一个成年男人的监护权。”

text:
PAUSE ADVANCED AI DEVELOPMENT BEFORE IT’S TOO LATE

If some of the world's leading scientists are concerned about artificial intelligence becoming independent of human control with potentially catastrophic results, shouldn't we do everything in our power to prevent it?

Nobel Prize winner Dr. Geoffrey Hinton, the Godfather of AI, says that AI poses a 10% to 20% chance of wiping out humanity.

Mark Winer, an AI safety and physics researcher: “AI is progressing much faster than we thought. It’s a difficult situation, and we don’t have answers. We could be heading toward a catastrophe.”

text:
路透社今天把 Anthropic（$ANT） 这场史上最大 IPO 的幕后细节全捅出来了，华尔街那帮平时眼高于顶的顶级投行，这回算是把尊严按在地上摩擦。

为了赚这笔 5 亿美元的承销费，投行吞下了一堆罕见的“霸王条款”：每家银行核心团队限死最多 4 个人；文件禁止保存 PDF，全打上员工个人水印防泄密；最绝的是逼着投行员工签个人排他协议，直接点名禁止他们服务 OpenAI、Cursor、DeepSeek 和 Hugging Face。

结果防泄密防得像谍战片，最后还是没防住，反倒是自家律所把定价和股数发错了，逼得 Anthropic 在纽约时间凌晨 2 点临时重发招股书，只留给华尔街几小时签字画押。

平时华尔街天天教育别人什么叫专业，真到了 5 亿美金摆在桌上，甲方凌晨两点发错文件照样得乖乖签字。顺便说一句，能让硅谷新王专门写进排他名单死防的，中国模型就点了 DeepSeek 一个名字——这波含金量，你怎么看？

路透社今天把 Anthropic（$ANT） 这场史上最大 IPO 的幕后细节全捅出来了，华尔街那帮平时眼高于顶的顶级投行，这回算是把尊严按在地上摩擦。

为了赚这笔 5 亿美元的承销费，投行吞下了一堆罕见的“霸王条款”：每家银行核心团队限死最多 4 个人；文件禁止保存 PDF，全打上员工个人水印防泄密；最绝的是逼着投行员工签个人排他协议，直接点名禁止他们服务 OpenAI、Cursor、DeepSeek 和 Hugging Face。

结果防泄密防得像谍战片，最后还是没防住，反倒是自家律所把定价和股数发错了，逼得 Anthropic 在纽约时间凌晨 2 点临时重发招股书，只留给华尔街几小时签字画押。

平时华尔街天天教育别人什么叫专业，真到了 5 亿美金摆在桌上，甲方凌晨两点发错文件照样得乖乖签字。顺便说一句，能让硅谷新王专门写进排他名单死防的，中国模型就点了 DeepSeek 一个名字——这波含金量，你怎么看？

text:
I finished the full week with Devin. I couldn't share the results day by day because of a few things that came up, but this is how the week actually went for me.

Honestly what I liked most about Devin this week is that it keeps opening up more options for me with as much stability as possible.

Devin shows off a lot of features like Devin Bots, cloud agents on Mac, Windows and Linux, security features and a lot more. But it actually delivers on most of them, and well enough that you can rely on them. Take GPT's Codex in the cloud. It's a disaster, it breaks all the time and it's unusable. I didn't run into anything like that with Devin.

With Grok Bot you feel boxed in because you can't pick the right model for each task. With Devin Bots you can pick from different models like Fable, Neon and SWE-2, and you can bring your ChatGPT subscription, connect it easily and use Astra and Sol. That variety makes working with the bots stronger, and the work they put out feels more reliable. They still need some improvement and customization, and I'll get into that in my full Devin Bots review soon.

Back to the main point.

On usage limits, you have to lean on SWE-2 and make it part of your workflow if you want the subscription to last the whole week. I won't lie to you, there was one full day I didn't use anything at all because I was busy, so I really used it for 6 days. I hit the weekly limit on the last day, but luckily I had credits so I finished my tasks.

For engineering and coding, SWE-2 is enough for 90% of use cases. It falls short on UI and 3D, but beyond that it's a capable model.

What's impressive is SWE-2 Lightning. You can use it heavily and you won't feel it eating through your limits, unlike Sol Ultra Fast, even though SWE-2 is faster than Sol Ultra Fast.

And look at the speed. OpenAI charges 6x your Sol usage for Sol Ultra Fast, and the speed isn't even impressive. Devin gives you SWE-2 at over 1,000 tokens per second for $5 per 1M output tokens. That's cheaper than even the Chinese models people know for being cheap. Now put that next to everything else Devin gives you.

A lot of you have been asking me if I recommend Devin over the others. To be completely honest and transparent with you:

Compared to the Chinese subscriptions, Devin wins 100%.

Compared to ChatGPT at the same price tier, Devin wins 100% too.

Compared to the unified X subscription, the $30 tier right now is more than enough to get Premium, verify your X account and use Grok Bot for X-related stuff. The $200 tier is kind of useless until a model stronger than Grok comes out. So Devin wins here too.

Compared to Google Ultra, it's a real fight and it comes down to preference, especially with Neon around. Nobody will give you more Neon than Google, and nobody will give you more SWE-2 than Cognition. But Devin has the edge of having different models in one place, so you get the strengths of each one at the same time.

You can't rely on all of them for both planning and execution though. Plan with a strong model and execute with cheaper, more efficient ones. Those models can execute just fine as long as there's a solid plan.

Here's something that improved the results of the execution models inside Devin for me. Have the most capable model, the one writing the plan, lay it out with a clear structure, an architecture diagram, deliverables and goals. That makes the task doable for the cheaper models, and inside Devin you can actually run those for days straight. That's where you get insane power.

Google does have its own edge right now, and the powerful GPUs it gives you play a big part. If you're developing models, leaning toward Google is an understandable call.

Claude is the hardest comparison for me. There are big differences between the two. Devin refuses a lot less, across every kind of task. I was translating a book because I wanted to read it in my native language. I used Devin, then gave the same prompt to Claude, Grok and Codex, and they all refused. Devin was the only one that agreed and did the work smoothly without stopping.

Of course Claude will be way more generous with Anthropic's models. That's true for all of them though. Each one is more generous with its own models only. Overall Devin is more generous.

Man they give you 4 cloud sessions of SWE-2. You can run all 4 at the same time for 24 hours straight and you'll almost never hit a limit. That's based on my own experience. Isn't that impressive?

Devin packs features and capabilities into one subscription that even $500 a month wouldn't cover anywhere else.

Where Devin really wins is that it gives you more varied options, plus features that used to be limited to companies and enterprises.

I'm really excited for the next SWE release. I don't know what model it'll be built on or what it'll be able to do, but I trust the jump between Devin releases because it's usually a big one.

There are a few things I want from Devin next. It would be great if I could pick every model available in local mode inside cloud mode too, instead of being limited to a few models. It would also be great if I could set the effort manually for each model in cloud mode.

I also want it to let me bring my own keys instead of using ACP. I want to see my models running inside Devin instead of in another harness, because Devin's harness is genuinely exceptional. Once I can bring my own keys, the Devin subscription kills every other one.

I really wish more people would try Devin themselves. I don't get why all people care about is how generous the limits are, instead of asking what features are there and thinking seriously about how to use them.

So try it. You've got nothing to lose. Even if you start with the $20 plan, get a feel for it. Talk to SWE-2, see what it can do, see how generous it is, see how well it engineers and how exceptionally it understands repos. Then decide if you want to upgrade to $200.

I fully recommend it. Not because I'm a Cognition ambassador, but because getting into their ecosystem and tools now will give you a competitive edge.

24 hours with Devin, day two.

I used Devin heavily today. I leaned a lot on Fable 5.2, one of the most expensive models in the world, plus some really heavy Blender work, and I had 3 sessions running at the same time. Every single task I had was fully on Devin from start to finish. Nothing happened outside of it.

The result: I burned about 24%. That was a very heavy day on Fable, so imagine it with cheaper models like Opus 5.5. Honestly not bad at all.

This isn't a normal day for me. I think I got two to three days of work done in one go today. So let's see how it looks over the next few days.

But so far, being able to run different models in the same harness this efficiently is a lot of fun.

That's day two. Stay tuned for tomorrow.

I really wish more people would try Devin themselves. I don't get why all people care about is how generous the limits are, instead of asking what features are there and thinking seriously about how to use them.

So try it. You've got nothing to lose. Even if you start with the $20 plan, get a feel for it. Talk to SWE-2, see what it can do, see how generous it is, see how well it engineers and how exceptionally it understands repos. Then decide if you want to upgrade to $200.

I fully recommend it. Not because I'm a Cognition ambassador, but because getting into their ecosystem and tools now will give you a competitive edge.

text:
这两天 T3 Code 突然火了，原因很简单

Gemini 4 好评如潮，订阅却被锁死在难用的 Antigravity 里。大家用反代绕过去，结果 magpie 这类项目第二天就被整批封号。

后来 Google 在官方论坛明确表态：只要运行官方原版 antigravity-acp、走它自带的登录，用于个人交互式开发，就是合规的。T3 Code 正是这么做的。

总结了下T3 的优势：

1、合法：别人走反代赌封号，它走官方通道，不用赌

2、不转卖 token：不额外收费，直接用你已有的 Claude / Codex / ChatGPT / Gemini 订阅

3、一个界面管所有 agent：Claude Code、Codex、Cursor、OpenCode、Antigravity 等全支持，对话中途还能切模型，让 Claude 把任务交接给 Codex

4、多端同步：桌面、网页、手机共享同一批 thread，手机上就能批准命令，人不在电脑前 agent 也能继续干活

5、内建 Git：每条 thread 独立 worktree，看 diff、commit、push、开 PR 一键完成

6、扩展快：基于 ACP 架构，新 agent 写个 adapter 就能接入，Gemini 4 一发布就跟上了

7、MIT 开源：约 7 万 star，代码和会话都在本地

适合：手上有多个 agent 订阅、想统一调度、需要用手机远程推进任务的人。

这两天大家都在看大厂用 AI 疯狂跑证明，昨天（11 月 22 号）MathOverflow 上有个帖子直接把另一面的残酷撕开了。

一位发展中国家的纯数学博士后在上面求助：他身边没有一个人买得起一个月 20 美元的 ChatGPT Plus，更别提更贵的科研版模型，自己至今还是拿纸笔推公式，现在到底该怎么接着发论文？

评论区有巴西学者算了笔账，20 到 200 美元的订阅费，在巴西相当于博士生一个月津贴的 5% 到 25%，而在美国连 1% 到 5% 都不到。
哪怕咬牙凑出钱，还可能被地区封锁拦在门外。与此同时有期刊编辑回帖说，现在靠 AI 把发文量拉高 5 倍的人挤爆了投稿系统，审稿人却越来越少，没用 AI 批量产稿的人反而成批被拒。

最有黑色幽默的是高赞第一条建议。英国莱斯特大学副教授、前 IMO 金牌得主 Bogdan Grechuk 直接甩出专门发 AI 论文的网站 Hexagon（上面不少论文直接标着人类理解度：仅部分），还贴了篇自己 10 月末挂上去的 AI 数论稿。
原话大意是：如果你感兴趣就联系我，我实在没时间把这份证明看懂。

他的方案是：有钱用 AI 的人负责批量跑出自己都还没读懂的证明，买不起 20 美元会员的学者负责帮他看懂、嚼碎、写成人类能读的版本去投期刊，俩人共同署名。
这大概就是学术圈刚冒出来的新分工吧。你们怎么看?👀

text:
It seems extremely dangerous to me from a security perspective that the current iteration of AI assistants (muse, grokbot, dots, instinct, etc) act directly on behalf of users by logging in as them (either directly in the browser or through oauth).

If we are really concerned about nefarious uses of AI (either by a bad actor or by an out of control AI), allowing agents to directly impersonate folks through their social accounts, emails, etc, seems like a recipe for disaster down the road. 

Imagine your friends getting emails and texts directly from your actual accounts that aren't written by you, or posts happening on your behalf to X, etc. This seems innocuous enough when those communications are agents scheduling meetings and that kind of thing, but it's a huge hole for potential future abuse where a compromised agent takes advantage of the trust relationships you have through your personal connections to achieve some bad goal.

We need some protocol for agents doing useful work that doesn't allow them to impersonate users directly. This doesn't just apply to consumer, it also matters for enterprise use cases like software factories.  We should always know when an agent is acting and not empower agents to act through human accounts.  Can't emphasize this enough.

菲尔兹奖得主 Borcherds 刚给自己下了个结论：

“AI 已经全面比我强了。做研究比我强，教书也比我强。照我的理解，已经没有理由再雇我了。”

Borcherds 是 1998 年的菲尔兹奖得主，数学界的最高奖，现在在伯克利教书。

他说眼下还有些事他比 AI 做得好，但撑不了太久。
在他看来，这是数学史上最大的事件，几百个重要难题突然一下子被解决了。这周 Anthropic 的数学家还刚说，自己和 Claude 一起证明了黎曼猜想。

最扎心的一句：
“意识到自己花了一辈子苦练的本事，AI 现在做得更好，确实有点让人不安。”

但他接下来的话把我看笑了。
他说其实也没多大区别。世界上本来就有很多比我强得多的数学家，以前比我强的有 N 个，现在变成 N+1 个，有什么大不了的？

我的看法是，这是我见过最体面的被 AI 超越的姿态。
普通人怕 AI，怕的是自己被比下去。顶尖的人早就习惯了头上有人，他们更在意题有没有解出来，谁解的没那么要紧。

反过来想，最慌的可能是那些一辈子没遇到过对手的人。 https://t.co/6U9AVFHuEh

英伟达董事会恢复黄仁勋的总裁、首席执行官及董事职务

2026年11月23日

英伟达（NASDAQ：NVDA）今日宣布，即日起，黄仁勋正式恢复担任公司总裁兼首席执行官，并重新成为董事会成员。

在与黄仁勋进行一系列讨论和会谈后，董事会一致投票决定恢复其职务。经过这些会谈，董事会对黄仁勋的坦诚态度及其领导英伟达的能力表示满意。

在作出这一决定的过程中，董事会征询了美国政府高级官员的意见。根据所获得的意见，董事会确信，黄仁勋的复职不会构成任何国家安全风险。

董事会主席哈维·琼斯（Harvey C. Jones）表示：

“董事会认为，黄仁勋是领导英伟达的最佳人选。他的复职符合公司股东、员工、合作伙伴及客户的最大利益。

我们对黄仁勋充满信心，期待他重新领导公司，与我们继续合作。

同时，我们感谢科莱特·克雷斯（Colette Kress）在担任临时首席执行官期间作出的杰出贡献。她也将继续履行英伟达首席财务官的职责。”

哈维·琼斯将继续担任董事会主席。

2001年，亚马逊股价暴跌80%，贝索斯却写下了一封后来成为投资史经典的股东信。

开头只有一个词：Ouch！（真疼！）

当时互联网泡沫破裂，整个市场都在质疑亚马逊能否活下去。

但贝索斯列出了一组完全相反的数据：

-股价暴跌80%，营收却增长68%，达到27.6亿美元。

-毛利润增长125%，达到6.56亿美元。

-用户数从1400万增长至2000万。

-经营亏损率从26%收窄至6%。

-账上还有11亿美元现金。

然后，他引用了格雷厄姆那句经典的话：

“短期来看，股市是投票机；长期来看，股市是称重机。”

此后，亚马逊股价从互联网泡沫时期的高点最大跌去约95%，但最终成为全球最有价值的公司之一。

-----------------------------------------------------------
原文：

亚马逊2000年度致股东信
杰夫·贝索斯（Jeff Bezos）｜2001年

致我们的股东：

哎哟！

对于资本市场中的许多人来说，过去这一年实在是太残酷了，亚马逊的股东当然也不例外。

截至我写下这封信时，我们的股价相比去年我给大家写信时，已经下跌了超过80%。

尽管如此，几乎从任何一个衡量标准来看，今天的亚马逊都比过去任何时候更加强大。

- 2000年，我们服务了2,000万名客户，而1999年为1,400万名。

- 2000年，我们的销售额达到27.6亿美元，而1999年为16.4亿美元。

- 2000年第四季度，调整口径下的经营亏损占销售额的比例，从1999年第四季度的26%下降至6%。

- 2000年第四季度，美国业务调整口径下的经营亏损占销售额的比例，从1999年同期的24%下降至2%。

- 2000年，每位客户的平均消费金额为134美元，同比增长19%。

- 2000年，我们的毛利润达到6.56亿美元，而1999年为2.91亿美元，同比增长125%。

- 2000年第四季度，近36%的美国客户购买了我们“非BMV”商店中的商品，例如电子产品、工具和厨房用品。（BMV指图书、音乐和录像产品。）

- 2000年，国际业务销售额达到3.81亿美元，而1999年为1.68亿美元。

- 2000年第四季度，我们帮助合作伙伴https://t.co/PMzoeMZ0iR销售了超过1.25亿美元的玩具和电子游戏产品。

- 截至2000年末，我们持有的现金及有价证券达到11亿美元，高于1999年末的7.06亿美元，这得益于我们在2000年初完成的可转换债券融资。

- 最重要的是，我们始终全心全意地关注客户，这一点体现在美国顾客满意度指数（American Customer Satisfaction Index）84分的成绩上。据我们了解，这是该指数有史以来任何行业的服务型公司所获得的最高分。

那么，如果今天公司的经营状况比一年前更好，为什么股价却比一年前低了这么多？

正如著名投资者本杰明·格雷厄姆所说：

“短期来看，股票市场是一台投票机；长期来看，它是一台称重机。”

显然，在1999年的繁荣时期，市场进行了大量的“投票”，却很少真正进行“称重”。

我们是一家希望接受“称重”的公司。

随着时间推移，我们终将接受这样的衡量——从长期来看，所有公司都会如此。

与此同时，我们会继续埋头苦干，努力打造一家越来越有分量的公司。

text:
Vercel Next.js 团队的老哥，烧了大概 60B tokens，最后就总结出一份 AGENTS.md，核心就 8 条规则。
60B tokens 什么概念？换算成钱，差不多六位数美元。
这 8 条规则说白了就一句话：别让你的 AI 编程助手像个刚入行的实习生，什么都想自己造一遍；要让它像干了十年的老油条一样，写最少的、最能用的代码。

直接上规则：
1. 不保留向后兼容。过时的东西直接删，别加兼容层、别写迁移脚本、别留备用回退方案。
2. 选能满足当前需求的最简单实现。别搞预防性抽象，也别加那些“万一以后用得上”的配置层。
3. 系统要分层生长。先跑通一个最小的端到端版本，能跑了再往上加东西。绝对不要因为未来可能出现的复杂度，就去拆掉一个当前能正常工作的东西。
4. 组件保持模块化，关注点要分离清楚。
5. 优先用成熟的、有人维护的第三方库。没有特别硬的理由，别自己重写。
6. 动手之前，先翻翻项目里已经有的依赖能做什么，再决定要不要加新包或自己写。别想当然地觉得库里肯定没有。
7. 架构决策要往长远做。不接受“先凑合用，以后再说”这种临时方案。
8. 先看成熟产品是怎么解决同一个问题的，用已经被验证过的模式，别从零开始发明。

就这 8 条，丢进你项目根目录的 AGENTS.md 文件里，Cursor、Claude Code、Codex、Windsurf 这些工具都会自动读取。
为什么它能省 token？因为 AI 写代码最大的浪费，其实不是写错，而是反复写多余的东西。
它给你引三个依赖、搭五个抽象层，解决一个标准库十行就能搞定的事；你让它改，它又给你补两百行。这 8 条规则就是在它动笔之前把它摁住：能不写的不写，能复用的复用，能简单的别搞复杂。
代码短了，返工少了，token 自然就省了。
之前我推荐过的 Ponytail 那个插件，干的是同一件事，只不过它是在运行时强制检查；而这个是在 AGENTS.md 里从源头约束。两个一起用，效果拔群。

但作者自己加了个非常实在的警告：
这套规则只适合 side projects，生产环境慎用。
他亲口说过，“不保留向后兼容”那条，曾经让 Agent 差点删了生产数据库的表，差点损失 2000 美元的数据。生产环境你得自己改，至少把第一条删掉，或者改得温和一点。
所以，如果你在做 side project、内部工具、原型，把这 8 条抄进 AGENTS.md，你会发现 AI 写出来的代码突然像个人写的了。
如果你要用在生产环境，自己把握好第一条和第七条之间的度，别让 AI 把你的库表删了。

省 token 的方法有很多——换便宜模型是一种，写好 prompt 是一种，但最有效的，是在项目根目录放一个文件，告诉 AI：
别整花活，写最少的、能跑的代码。

🚨 BREAKING: COLETTE KRESS BLASTS NVIDIA OVER JENSEN HUANG’S REINSTATEMENT, ACCUSES THE COMPANY OF HAVING NO INTEGRITY AND QUESTIONS ITS LEADERSHIP!

Colette Kress has reacted angrily to NVIDIA’s decision to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO, criticizing the company’s leadership and questioning the integrity of the decision-making process.

Kress expressed disappointment over the way the situation was handled, arguing that a company of NVIDIA’s global reputation should not make major leadership decisions without transparency, accountability and respect for everyone involved.

She described the decision as a serious reflection of the company’s internal culture, insisting that integrity should never become optional simply because someone holds an influential position.

COLETTE KRESS’ STATEMENT:

“Quite frankly, I find this entire situation disappointing. NVIDIA cannot continue presenting itself as a company built on excellence, innovation and integrity while making decisions that raise serious questions about its leadership and corporate values.

“You cannot disregard people, undermine accountability and expect everyone to remain silent when decisions are made behind closed doors. A company’s reputation is not built on its market value or technological achievements alone. It is built on trust, transparency and the principles it claims to represent.

“Reinstating Jensen Huang does not automatically erase the questions surrounding everything that happened. If NVIDIA genuinely believes in integrity, then it must demonstrate that through its actions, not just its public statements.

“No individual is bigger than the company, and no company should consider itself above accountability. NVIDIA needs to explain its decisions and stop treating serious concerns as though they do not matter.”

Her comments have added another layer of controversy to the NVIDIA leadership story, raising questions about corporate accountability, internal trust and the company’s direction moving forward.

You helped build a company that has become one of the most influential names in the technology industry. text:
袁腾飞在直播里聊美国的生活成本，说了一句很实在的话：

在美国，东西只要不用人，便宜得跟白给一样；只要一用人，就是天价。

他买过最便宜的一件T恤，两块九毛九美元，合人民币14块钱，质量比国内更贵的衣服还好。

给孩子买双皮鞋，原价30多美元，打折后结账，一块零七分。他以为算错了。一双皮鞋，还没一瓶可乐贵——可乐要两块六毛九。

可马桶堵了，得自己掏；轮胎没气了，跟房东借个气筒，自己打。在国内随手找个师傅就能办的事，在那边请人又贵又慢。

他说自己是文科生，动手能力极差，这也是他这么多年，一直不敢去美国的原因之一。

反过来，美国的体力活是真挣钱。送快递的一年十几万美元，建筑工人一年12万，垃圾清运工一个月上22天班，到手6000美元。

有一对福建父子，在美国开大货车，晚上就睡在车上，三年攒下一千万人民币，回国了。

他的结论是：美国适合肯出力气的人，也适合有钱人，就是中产要慎重。挣工资的，税一笔一笔记得清清楚楚，躲不掉。

听完挺感慨的。东西便宜的地方，人贵；人不值钱的地方，日子也未必好过。

她本来想当模特，败在了一口东北方言上。

转头她就去拍AV了，还成了S1最显眼的长腿。

她就是明日叶美津羽，175cm，F罩杯，2000年出生，东北人。来东京四年之后，2023年7月以S1专属的身份出道，出道的理由是憧憬三上悠亚。

175cm的身高本来是她想当模特的本钱，结果东北口音怎么都改不掉，模特那条路走不通。出道的时候，口音和身高都是她的心结，拍着拍着反而成了招牌：长身一站出来，什么体位都好看，戏里一开口，东北腔一出来，又憨又可爱，反差直接拉满。

FANZA的编辑部评价她很有意思：拍玩法的片子，靠长身带来的动态身体取胜；拍剧情片，端庄的外表配上不太靠谱的演技和改不掉的口音，反而成了可爱的地方。

2024年她开始爆发，相部屋NTR、温泉旅行纪录片轮着上租赁榜，7月拿了FANZA租赁月榜女优第5位。2025年3月的水泳部顾问NTR首周租赁第3位。2026年8月，她移籍到了IdeaPocket。

代表作：

1. SSIS-906｜激イキ162回！痙攣4480回！イキ潮1630cc！エロス覚醒 はじめての大・痙・攣スペシャル｜S1
出道三个月后的痉挛特辑，162次高潮、4480次痉挛，FANZA上61人打分，是她评价最高的一部。

2. SONE-107｜SEXの天才 明日葉みつはが底なしの性欲を満たす為のプライベート絶倫温泉旅行ドキュメント｜S1
底なし性欲的温泉旅行纪录片，35人打分，私密感最强的一部。

3. SSIS-818｜新人NO.1 STYLE 明日葉みつはAVDebut｜S1
出道作，2023年7月11日，95人打分，东北口音从第一部就没藏着。

4. SONE-793｜上半身は仕事着、下半身は丸出しでリモート会議するズボラお姉ちゃんの半裸在宅勤務がたまらない！！｜S1
上半身正装、下半身全裸开远程会议，13人打分但全是高分，设定最离谱的一部。

5. SONE-439｜優しくて自慢の長身彼女が水泳部顧問の性指導で寝取られた。｜S1

text:
I'm a spine surgeon. You asked a fair question, so here's the plain-English answer.

Before 2012 you could buy an individual plan online for about $200 a month, pick from six or seven insurers, and choose your own deductible: $500 if you wanted to pay more up front, $5,000 if you didn't. If you were healthy, that is. If you were sick, they could turn you down, and that part was real and had to be fixed.

Obamacare fixed it by requiring every plan to cover everyone for everything. Good. But that made the real price of a plan jump, and the only way to keep the monthly number from looking insane was to push the cost onto the back end. That's your $6,500 deductible. You're paying comprehensive prices for catastrophic coverage.

Then the quiet part. The law caps what insurers can keep at 20% of premiums. So the only way an insurer makes more money is if the total bill gets bigger. 20% of $10,000 beats 20% of $5,000. They have no reason to fight the hospital's price. They pass it through, take their cut, and send you the premium.

And the hospital's price went up. Hospitals bought the independent doctors, and the same visit & surgery under the hospital's name now costs  3-10 times more. Hospital prices are up 281% since 2000. 

The number of insurers you can choose from fell to one in half the counties in America by 2018. Meanwhile, six in ten adults now have a chronic disease, so the pool is sicker.

So: sicker patients, pricier hospitals, an insurer that profits from a bigger bill, and a law that moved the cost to your deductible. That's what you're paying for.

Nobody in that chain gets paid more if you get better. That's the part to fix.

text:
MCP as you know it is cooked.

@Cloudflare just showed you can give an agent their entire API, 2,500+ endpoints, in about 1,000 tokens.

The old way: every endpoint becomes its own MCP tool. Load all 2,594 and the tool definitions alone eat around 1.17 million tokens, more than most models' entire context window.

Code Mode flips it:

- The server exposes just 2 tools, search() and execute()
- The agent writes JavaScript to search the API spec and find what it needs
- Then it writes one script that chains the calls together
- That code runs in an isolated sandbox, and only the result comes back

Same access. 99.9% fewer tokens.

Anthropic explored the same pattern with code execution and programmatic tool calling for Claude.

The future of agent tools is less tool calling and more code writing.

https://t.co/NeIjs9l4IS

text:
全网都在转 OpenAI 首次公开预训练指标、呼吁全行业限速，其实大多停在表面。
o1/o3 底座实锤、GPT-4.5 封神、5.5 之后模型越来越大，右下角还藏着个没放的 0.732。几条最值得看的 

1/ 先看第一个猛料：官方变相实锤了 o1 和 o3 的底座，也封神了 GPT-4.5。

图表直接把节点标成了 GPT-4o / o1 和 GPT-4.1 / o3。这基本等于 OpenAI 亲自确认：o1 和 o3 其实都是基于 GPT-4o 这一代基础模型跑出来的（4.1 则是其中的一个中间训练版本）。
更让人感慨的是 GPT-4.5 的位置——在 GPT-5.5 出来之前，没有任何一个模型在预训练底座上能明显打败 GPT-4.5。难怪大家看完直呼“GPT-4.5 is the GOAT”。

2/ 第二，4.5 之后路线明显变了，模型看起来越来越大。

在这之前，能力提升主要靠推理和强化学习，底座基本没往前走：从 GPT-4 到 GPT-5.2，将近三年，困惑度只降了 0.025。

5.5 以后就不一样了。5.5、5.6 Sol、6、6.2 都是新的 base model，而且从曲线的斜率看，一个比一个大。（OpenAI 钱烧得更快，感觉也跟预训练滚得太快有关？）
Pachocki 在脚注里也说，2026 年曲线急剧加速，主要来自长期研究和算力投入。预训练的 scaling，远没有撞墙。

3/ 第三，图的最右下角还画了一个尚未发布的 Internal model，0.732。

从 GPT-3.5 一路画到 GPT-6.2 Astra 还不算，最后还特意点上这么一个点，意思很明显：自己手里还有更强的没放呢（那你倒是拿出来呀🙂）。

4/ 聊完图里的猛料，再回头看 Pachocki 这篇文章真正想讲的底层逻辑：大模型就是对世界的压缩，但谁说压缩就不会产生超级智能？

外行看今天的 AI，总觉得它和传统软件工程一样，是一堆针对不同功能的复杂模块拼出来的。Pachocki 说不是，现代 AI 的主线非常简单粗暴：
造底座：搭一台超级计算机，往里灌海量非结构化数据，训练出一个超强“压缩器”（能把数据压缩到极致，等价于能最准确地预测下一个字/token）。他以前把这个底座形容为“外星心智”，很难解释它内部怎么运作，也不知道到底藏了多少潜力。

挖潜力：再用提示词、微调、强化学习等手段，把底座里已经潜伏的能力“逼”出来。

所以决定 AI 天花板的底层智能，核心就看一件事：预测下一个 token 到底有多准。衡量它的指标就是困惑度，数值越低，说明模型对世界规律压缩得越彻底。

5/ 基于这条曲线，Pachocki 还抛出了一个更大胆的外推：数学的今天，可能就是 2027 年深度学习的明天。

曲线降到 0.76 这一档时，模型开始接连解出数学界的开放难题。数学上刚发生的这一幕，让他觉得同样的突变很可能很快会在深度学习研究里重演。

虽然深度学习比纯数学更依赖做实验，但回顾历史，这个领域里“简单的好想法被人类错过好几年”的例子并不算少。一旦模型也开始在这个环节发力，最早到 2027 年，基础预训练研究就可能迎来类似“雪崩”式的加速。

6/ 最后说句实在话，其实我不太想讨论 AI 加速。很多人觉得这个是噱头，因为 AI 貌似还是没有解决生产力的问题，市面上“AI 要泡沫了”的声音也越来越大。在这种气氛下，任何喊“AI 要加速”的话，都很容易被直接归成又一套拉估值、卖焦虑的硅谷叙事。
但哪怕把这些叙事滤掉，Pachocki 这次切入的角度依然有讨论的价值。他没有去扯那种很科幻、很遥远的“完全递归自我改进”，而是落到了一个具体得多的环节：根本不需要脱离人类，只要 AI 能深度切入“预训练算法研究”这一件事，研发节奏本身就可能出现一次陡峭的跃迁。

不管你信与不信，至少这件事本身，值得我们持续关注。

更让人感慨的是 GPT-4.5 的位置——在 GPT-5.5 出来之前，没有任何一个模型在预训练底座上能明显打败 GPT-4.5。难怪大家看完直呼“GPT-4.5 is the GOAT”。

2/ 第二，4.5 之后路线明显变了，模型看起来越来越大。

在这之前，能力提升主要靠推理和强化学习，底座基本没往前走：从 GPT-4 到 GPT-5.2，将近三年，困惑度只降了 0.025。

5.5 以后就不一样了。5.5、5.6 Sol、6、6.2 都是新的 base model，而且从曲线的斜率看，一个比一个大。（OpenAI 钱烧得更快，感觉也跟预训练滚得太快有关？）
Pachocki 在脚注里也说，2026 年曲线急剧加速，主要来自长期研究和算力投入。预训练的 scaling，远没有撞墙。

3/ 第三，图的最右下角还画了一个尚未发布的 Internal model，0.732。

从 GPT-3.5 一路画到 GPT-6.2 Astra 还不算，最后还特意点上这么一个点，意思很明显：自己手里还有更强的没放呢（那你倒是拿出来呀🙂）。

4/ 聊完图里的猛料，再回头看 Pachocki 这篇文章真正想讲的底层逻辑：大模型就是对世界的压缩，但谁说压缩就不会产生超级智能？

外行看今天的 AI，总觉得它和传统软件工程一样，是一堆针对不同功能的复杂模块拼出来的。Pachocki 说不是，现代 AI 的主线非常简单粗暴：
造底座：搭一台超级计算机，往里灌海量非结构化数据，训练出一个超强“压缩器”（能把数据压缩到极致，等价于能最准确地预测下一个字/token）。他以前把这个底座形容为“外星心智”，很难解释它内部怎么运作，也不知道到底藏了多少潜力。

挖潜力：再用提示词、微调、强化学习等手段，把底座里已经潜伏的能力“逼”出来。

所以决定 AI 天花板的底层智能，核心就看一件事：预测下一个 token 到底有多准。衡量它的指标就是困惑度，数值越低，说明模型对世界规律压缩得越彻底。

5/ 基于这条曲线，Pachocki 还抛出了一个更大胆的外推：数学的今天，可能就是 2027 年深度学习的明天。

曲线降到 0.76 这一档时，模型开始接连解出数学界的开放难题。数学上刚发生的这一幕，让他觉得同样的突变很可能很快会在深度学习研究里重演。

虽然深度学习比纯数学更依赖做实验，但回顾历史，这个领域里“简单的好想法被人类错过好几年”的例子并不算少。一旦模型也开始在这个环节发力，最早到 2027 年，基础预训练研究就可能迎来类似“雪崩”式的加速。

6/ 最后说句实在话，其实我不太想讨论 AI 加速。很多人觉得这个是噱头，因为 AI 貌似还是没有解决生产力的问题，市面上“AI 要泡沫了”的声音也越来越大。在这种气氛下，任何喊“AI 要加速”的话，都很容易被直接归成又一套拉估值、卖焦虑的硅谷叙事。
但哪怕把这些叙事滤掉，Pachocki 这次切入的角度依然有讨论的价值。他没有去扯那种很科幻、很遥远的“完全递归自我改进”，而是落到了一个具体得多的环节：根本不需要脱离人类，只要 AI 能深度切入“预训练算法研究”这一件事，研发节奏本身就可能出现一次陡峭的跃迁。

不管你信与不信，至少这件事本身，值得我们持续关注。

text:
接着上一条聊一个更反直觉的事实。如果 P=NP 真的成立，我们其实根本不用等以后有人发明出那个快速算法，因为这个算法在 1973 年就已经写出来了，核心逻辑几十行代码就能实现。

这个算法叫列文通用搜索，提出它的人正是 NP 完全理论的奠基人之一列文（Leonid Levin）。它针对的是有解的 NP 搜索问题，思路非常直接。

具体做法是把所有可能存在的程序按代码长度从小到大排好，再交替并行运行，越短的程序分到的计算时间越多。每当某个程序跑出一个结果，就立刻用验证器检查答案对不对，验证通过就直接结束并输出结果。

这套做法神奇的地方在于，假设世界上真的存在一个极快的多项式时间算法，哪怕人类现在完全不知道它长什么样，它本质上也是一段有限长度的代码，一定会排在那个程序列表里。虽然列文通用搜索把大量时间花在了无数没用的程序上，但分给这个最快程序的时间比例是一个固定常数，只取决于这段代码有多长，不会随着输入规模变大而变化。

也就是说，只要 P=NP 成立，这个 1973 年就公开的算法本身就是多项式时间的，在时间复杂度上和那个未知的最快算法只差一个常数倍。

至于为什么现实里没人用它，原因和上一条里高德纳说的很像。那个常数大约是 2 的程序长度次方，就算最快的算法只需要 125 字节也就是 1000 比特就能写完，2 的 1000 次方也远远超过了可观测宇宙里的原子总数。理论上它快得惊人，现实里放到宇宙毁灭都跑不完。

其实这也很像现在用 AI 写代码的底层逻辑。列文通用搜索相当于没有方向地遍历所有程序，全靠验证器筛出正确答案，代价是常数大到无法运行。现在的大模型走的是同一套生成加验证的流程，区别在于模型通过训练学会了代码的分布规律，可以直接优先生成最可能正确的版本，再交给测试用例去验证，把原本天文数字一样的搜索代价压到了现实里能接受的范围。

quotedTweet.text:
聊到 P vs NP 问题，计算机科学界绝大多数人都认为 P 不等于 NP，所以很多人以为支持 P=NP 只是外行的猜测。但其实历史上和现在都有非常重量级的学者表达过支持 P=NP 的观点。

最早的是数学家哥德尔。1956 年他在写给冯诺依曼的一封信里，第一次提出了等价于 P vs NP 的问题。他在信里认为，快速求解的算法是完全有可能存在的，并且指出如果这件事成立，数学家做是非判断的脑力劳动就可以完全被机器取代。

另一位很知名的是图灵奖得主高德纳（Donald Knuth）。他在公开访谈里直接说过，他倾向于认为 P=NP 是成立的。他觉得多项式时间的算法有无数种可能，证明它们全都不存在非常困难，相反证明存在这样的算法更有可能。

不过高德纳也补充了一个很关键的看法。他觉得就算以后真的证明了 P=NP，这件事在现实里大概率也没有实用价值。因为那个证明很可能只是在理论上证明了算法存在，却没法告诉大家怎么写出这个算法，或者就算写出了这个算法，它的计算量也大到计算机根本没法运行。

所以支持 P=NP 并不是什么奇怪的想法。只是就算有一天大家真的证明了 P=NP，结果也很可能像高德纳预测的那样，在理论上意义很大，但不会立刻改变大家的正常生活。

Looking back, I may have moved too quickly, and I don’t want to rush into another major decision. For now, I’d like to take some time to rest, reflect, and think carefully about my future. As part of that, I’m open to exploring the possibility of returning.

Thank you for all the kindness and encouragement. Whatever comes next, I want to approach it with a clearer mind and give it the thought it deserves.

text:
「酱油」一词为什么正在被「生抽」和「老抽」替代？

给蚝油起名字叫蚝油的人，一定是一个伟大的产品经理。

说明他不仅了解添加剂，更加了解消费者，了解人。

蚝油蚝油，那自然是生蚝熬制的，是纯天然的。

棕褐色的膏状让人联想到古法传统制作的各种祖传秘方，一看配料表，真有蚝哎！

便放心大胆的吃了。

相反，给味精起名字叫“味精”的人，就是理工科直男了。

居然还敢把产品形状搞成白色小长粒结晶！简直是让老爸老妈睡不着觉了。

俺们老百姓别的不懂，就知道老祖宗传下来的放心，自然界存在的放心。

化工合成的不放心，名字陌生的不放心。

味精从发明以来最幸运的一点，就是没有直接叫“谷氨酸钠”这个恐怖的名字。

那简直是自绝销路、自绝于消费者了。

你看，自从味精可以被买到以来，引发了多少“味精有没有害”的讨论？

你什么时候见到有人讨论“酱油是否有害”？

什么时候见到有人讨论“鸡粉是否有害”？

最近逛超市，还有叫“松茸鲜”的产品，就简直不知道高到哪里去了。

你得学会帮爷爷奶奶们过心理上这关啊！得学会说漂亮话啊，得学会善意的哄啊。爷爷奶奶爸爸妈妈们要的是啥？

既要工业化的廉价便利，也要“天然”“手工”“古法”“已知熟悉事物”带来的心理慰藉和信仰加成。

渣男为什么总能有女朋友？就是因为人家能把对象哄开心啊。谁有心思听你讲道理？人家要的是情绪价值。

“酱油”为什么被生抽和老抽替代了？因为有些菜只需要谷氨酸钠提鲜，有些菜只需要焦糖色染色，但又不能直接卖这两种商品......

你在超市拿起一瓶酱油，瓶身上写着"生抽"。旁边那瓶写着"老抽"。两个都是酱油，但名字完全不同。你可能从来没想过一个问题：

这俩词，是哪儿来的？

答案是广东。

生抽、老抽，压根不是什么全国通用的酱油分类标准。这是一套来自粤语区的酿造术语，最后跟着广东酱油一起，占领了全中国的厨房。

广东酿酱油的历史可以追溯到明清。那时候珠三角气候湿热、日照充足，天然适合做露天日晒发酵。广东人酿酱油用的是"高盐稀态发酵"——黄豆（或脱脂大豆）蒸熟、拌入面粉制曲，然后投进大缸，加高浓度盐水，就这么在太阳底下晒上三个月、半年、甚至一年。每天有人来翻缸、抽油、回淋。日晒夜露，慢慢把蛋白质降解成氨基酸，把淀粉转化成糖。最后得到的那一缸酱汁，颜色透亮、鲜味足、有层次感。

这个过程里有个关键操作，叫"抽"——就是从发酵缸里把酱汁抽出来。

第一次抽出来的，色浅、味鲜、咸度适中，广东人叫它"生抽"。

抽完之后，剩下的酱醪还可以继续晒、继续发酵。等到颜色变深、质地变稠，再抽一次。这一次出来的酱油明显更浓、更黑、更挂壁，就叫"老抽"。有的老抽还会额外加焦糖色来强化上色能力。

再往细里分，还有"头抽"——整缸酱醪第一次抽取的最精华部分。头抽鲜度最高、产量最少，是酱油里的"头茬"。有的广东老牌酱油厂（比如东古、致美斋）至今还单独出头抽产品，价格比普通生抽贵一截。

所以你看，生抽、老抽、头抽——这整套叫法，全部来自"抽"这个动作。这是广东酱油作坊几百年来的行话，本质上描述的是同一缸酱醪在不同发酵阶段和不同抽取次数下的产物。

那北方呢？

北方传统上酿酱油用的是另一套工艺，叫"低盐固态发酵"。这种方法发酵周期短，通常一两个月就能出厂。因为加的盐少、水也少、发酵温度比较高，所以出来的酱油在口味上偏咸、偏直接，酱香味重但鲜味和层次感不如广式高盐稀态。也不存在分批次"抽"的操作，所以根本没有"生抽""老抽"这套概念。

北方人过去买酱油就是打酱油——拎着瓶子去副食店，从大缸里舀。那时候全国大部分地区的酱油都是散装的，黑乎乎一种，没什么品牌意识，也没有那么多细

Seeing a lot of confusion so let's make this very clear:

You can only use your Gemini subscription in Antigravity. T3 Code uses Antigravity. Other harnesses (i.e. Pi) do not use Antigravity, so they are not allowed.

T3 Code -> Antigravity binary -> Google API ✅
Pi -> (fake antigravity shim) -> Google API ❌

IMO this is pretty clear (same way that Claude subs work)

text:
Going into 2027 if you
• Are using a capable harness
• Understand the problem you're trying to solve
• Are able to clearly break down that problem

You should no longer be managing (or even having to think about) skills, context, verification, /goal, automations, memory, plugins, connectors, subagents, ... other plumbing.

Your harness should be capable enough to manage all of these things for you.

Skills specifically are increasingly unnecessary, counterproductive, and becoming an old-school artifact, only needed for edge cases (and what I'd consider the new version of code smell).

This is great because it eliminates most of the mental overhead we can now use purely focused on problem solving.

text:
I've been using GLM-5.4 for a while and I can confidently say that it's the best Open Model you can use right now.

It places itself at #7 on KingBench 4 which is the #1 Open Model placement.

From what I can tell, the model is an honest effort and isn't very benchmaxxed or stuff like that and it has good vibes (just don't look at the reasoning tokens... you feel sad for the model at times)

As much as I know it's a looped transformer with 700B params and a technical report shall come later.

It's the most careful model that I have ever used... It has found out many bugs and security vulns in my apps that others haven't (incl. Fable). That's not say that it's the best either. The model takes a lot of time to reach a conclusion to a task especially the Max effort can make it spiral down for a while.

It is on average about 4x slower than Neon on Max reasoning effort. At Medium reasoning effort this does indeed but at the cost of performance. High is the best sweet spot for me.

It isn't slow because of TPS btw.. KingBench 4 took 431 minutes against Neon's 109. Each step isn't slower (22.9 s, against 26.7 s for Neon); it just takes far more of them, 1,128 against 244. It also reasoned 1.04M tokens against Neon's roughly 0.07M. About three-quarters of its time is spent generating and a quarter running builds and tests.

I wouldn't recommend you to just use this model but keeping it as a reviewer for work and making it work on more complex architecture or searching for bugs, security vulnerabilities is really worth it imo.

This is a model that you can use end-to-end on work without much issues but it isn't the best or SOTA. 

I have it in my council of reviewers at all time before shipping anything and I am really happy about that.

How it behaves:

It reasons on almost every step. Under 1% of its steps have near-zero reasoning, against 14–39% for the GPT models. Max gives about 1.5× the reasoning of High.

It overthinks. On a security task, High and Max both hit the 180 s timeout while still thinking, and Medium passed in 95 s.

Tool errors are mid-pack. It fails 1.56% of tool calls across all harnesses, 11th of 17, and most of the failures are bad arguments to the edit tool. 

It recovers well, though: 66% of failed calls are followed by a working retry, better than every Claude and Codex model.

Caching is excellent at 96–99%, and median time to first token is quick at 4.1 s.

Here's when you should use it:
- You don't care about 3d or Frontend
- You care a lot about shipping no bugs or security vulns. then either make it write it's own code and also review it with a council or just keep it as a reviewer
- You need a really good planner for your work
- You need a model that gets the bigger picture (it's hard to explain but it gets the bigger picture of a work much better than others)

I like the vibes with this model and can't wait for what a bigger model with similar arch can do.

PandaCode's Orchestrator uses it where it should for you automatically.. so, you can plug it in and see some better results with orchestration overall: https://t.co/2S9H2IWsMD

Also, a thanks to the @Zai_org team for letting me be 100% honest about the model and it's vibes. This review or anything isn't sponsored in any way btw it's all my own thoughts and they haven't seen any of this before your eyes.

Full Review video here: https://t.co/PameGfAl0N

拍卖原版冠军车，最高出价只有250
于是自己300万拍了，扣下来了

——这是妥妥的黄毛思维：
我认为对的，就是对的，我就要去贯彻、执行到底

黄毛思维贯彻张雪的前半生：
1，19岁对记者死缠烂打，求上电视台
2，24岁结婚一分钱彩礼不掏，也要把初恋娶回家
3，26岁重庆创业，让妻子借遍娘家人，直到2024年才还清

4，39岁一战成名，果断拉黑“蹭流量”的亲妈，不内耗
5，本承诺拍卖的钱给韩红基金会，结果公开变卦，要捐给小车手

——黄毛思维，让张雪从底层一路厮杀上来，稳住了自己的江山

但一个人一举成名，成为公众人物后
要做的应该是收敛、言出必行
而不是按性子办事，凸显个性
这样才能越做越好

当然，这个故事的具体真相怎样，有何苦衷
还得看张雪后续怎么说了
